evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background Assisted reproductive technology (ART) management relies on hormone measurements whose review requires integration of cycle stage, treatment regimen, medication context, and longitudinal hormone history. Manual review demands specialist expertise and sustained attention, potentially limiting efficiency and consistency at high testing volumes. We developed NovaMind, a task-specific large language model (LLM) for patient-level plausibility review of ART hormone results, and explored patient-based real-time quality control (PBRTQC) for complementary system-level monitoring. Methods This study included 5,852 patients and 10,526 review units. Retrospective data collected from 21 May 2020 to 28 February 2026 were partitioned by patient for model development and internal evaluation. NovaMind underwent two-stage supervised fine-tuning and was evaluated against an expert-derived reference standard. Input ablation assessed the contribution of longitudinal hormone history. Prospective evaluation from 1 March to 1 May 2026 included 1,435 consecutive review units in a silent cohort and a challenge set comprising 900 real-world negative units and 100 data-augmented abnormal units. PBRTQC was evaluated using simulated shifts in retrospective data and operated silently on prospective result streams. Results In the internal test set, NovaMind reduced the false-negative rate (FNR) by 11.00 percentage points and increased the negative predictive value (NPV) by 10.30 percentage points compared with conventional autoverification. Adding longitudinal hormone history reduced the FNR from 30.00% to 21.00% and increased the NPV from 90.51% to 93.46%. In the challenge set, NovaMind detected 77 of 100 data-augmented abnormal units and correctly classified 705 of 900 real-world negative units. All 1,435 units in the prospective silent cohort were reference-negative, among which NovaMind achieved 81.95% specificity (95% CI, 79.88%–83.85%).
evidence_items.title: A longitudinally informed large language model for patient-level review of hormone test results in assisted reproductive technology: development, internal testing, and prospective silent evaluation

organizations: Department of Computer Science and Electronics, Universitas Gadjah Mada, Yogyakarta, Indonesia
Vienna University of Economics and Business
evidence_items.summary: Advancements in large language models (LLMs) offer opportunities for automating challenging and time-intensive Knowledge Engineering (KE) tasks. Constructing an ontology is particularly complex when modeling logical axioms, especially among novice knowledge engineers and domain experts with limited KE training. Consequently, ontologies often contain modeling errors, undermining ontology-based applications and hindering subsequent KE tasks. Thus, it is important to investigate how LLMs can support KE tasks such as the evaluation of ontologies. However, systematically evaluating LLM performance remains challenging due to a lack of comprehensive, task-specific benchmarks needed for such LLM capability assessments. As a result, selecting the right LLM to support knowledge engineers is nontrivial. This study investigates how LLMs can support four concrete ontology evaluation subtasks: detection, classification, explanation, and possible correction of modeling issues, focusing on the use of existential, universal, and cardinality property restrictions. We construct a benchmark of student-built ontologies and assess the performance of four LLMs—GPT-4o, ClaudeSonnet, DeepSeekV3, and Llama3.3—on these KE subtasks. Additionally, we exemplify an annotation framework for qualitatively evaluating LLM outputs and analyse the capabilities of each model. Our findings reveal differences in model behavior and task-specific strengths, underscoring the importance of selecting an appropriate model for each KE task.
evidence_items.title: Knowledge Engineering With Large Language Models: A Capability Assessment in Evaluating Ontology Property Restrictions
BRAVO Benchmark: Evaluating MLLMs for BIM Scene-Based Compliance Checking

organizations: Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Multidisciplinary Innovations, College of Accounting, University of South Africa, Pretoria 0002, South Africa
evidence_items.summary: Large language models such as GPT-4, Med-PaLM 2, and BioMedLM are being increasingly applied to clinical decision support tasks including diagnostic reasoning, clinical documentation, medical question answering, and patient-facing health communication, with several studies reporting performance comparable to trained clinicians on structured benchmarks. However, the current pace of adoption has outrun the critical evaluation of whether these models are genuinely safe, equitable, and sustainable for deployment in real-world healthcare environments. This narrative review argues that the existing literature has focused disproportionately on benchmark performance while giving insufficient attention to the conditions required for these models to function as trustworthy long-term clinical tools. Drawing on published evidence across medical informatics, clinical artificial intelligence, and natural language processing, we synthesise model performance across four clinical task areas and examine documented limitations including factual hallucination, demographic bias, and poor generalisability outside controlled settings that are already present in current deployments. We further identify five structural sustainability challenges that obstruct responsible deployment at scale, and propose a corresponding five-pillar framework alongside a priority research agenda for closing the gaps this review identifies. This review contributes a critically grounded perspective to the growing discourse on artificial intelligence for sustainable healthcare, with direct relevance to Sustainable Development Goal 3 (Good Health and Well-Being) and Sustainable Development Goal 10 (Reduced Inequalities), and offers concrete guidance for developing clinical models that are safe, inclusive, and viable across diverse global health contexts.
evidence_items.title: Large Language Models in Clinical Decision Support: A Critical Review of Progress, Limitations, and the Path Toward Sustainable Healthcare

evidence_items.summary: The intelligent transformation of industrial robots is extending inspection from conventional mechanical-performance tests to the evaluation of perception, decision-making, learning, and human–robot interaction. This review summarizes artificial intelligence (AI)-driven robot inspection from two complementary perspectives. First, AI is examined as an inspection tool for appearance-defect recognition, visual trajectory measurement, anomaly detection, online health assessment, and remaining-useful-life prediction, with attention to lightweight and edge-deployment techniques. Second, AI-enabled intelligence is treated as the inspection target, covering visual and force perception, autonomous planning, robustness to distribution shifts, continual-learning stability, and collaborative behavior. The principal obstacles to production deployment are then analyzed, including scarce and imbalanced data, insufficient cross-model generalization, false alarms, real-time constraints, limited interpretability, and the absence of standardized datasets and model-validation procedures. Future research should emphasize inspection-specific efficient architectures, physics–data hybrid models, explainable evidence chains, multimodal foundation models, and lifecycle-oriented standards. These developments are necessary to convert laboratory accuracy into reliable, reproducible, and certifiable performance in industrial environments.
evidence_items.title: Artificial intelligence-driven inspection technologies for industrial robots
RDFS-LLM-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating RDF Schema Inference in LLMs
SSIB: A Security-Centric Benchmark and Multi-agent Framework for Detecting Stablecoin-Specific Vulnerabilities

organizations: Linkou Senior High School, Suzhou Industrial Park ,  Suzhou .  Jiangsu ,  P.R.China ,  215021
evidence_items.summary: The growing application of big‑data technologies has made official statistics a critical basis for macroeconomic judgment and public policy formulation. Existing scholarly work mostly concentrates on deliberate data falsification induced by administrative interventions and performance‑oriented incentives, while systematic discussions about unintentional distortions stemming from technical factors remain fragmented. This paper distinguishes technical statistical distortion from intentional human data manipulation. Based on literature‑driven qualitative analysis, this paper sorts out typical forms of technical distortion amid big‑data scenarios, and identifies four major technical root causes: flawed statistical planning, outdated data collection and input procedures, non‑standard computational algorithms and insecure distributed data storage. The paper proposes targeted preventive strategies in four areas: source‑end scheme optimization, intelligent audit system upgrade, standardized data processing routines and traceable storage architecture construction. Research outcomes indicate that institutional adjustment alone cannot completely eliminate technical distortion; multilevel technical governance must span the full data lifecycle to reduce systematic bias in statistical outputs. This study offers practical references for enhancing data quality under large‑scale multi‑source data environments.
evidence_items.title: Technical distortions of statistical data in the big‑data era: causes and countermeasures

organizations: Arab Academy for Science, Technology, and Maritime Transport
evidence_items.summary: Abstract As modern systems evolve into complex microservices and highly regulated data ecosystems, manual test case design has become a severe bottleneck in Agile CI/CD pipelines. While Artificial Intelligence (AI) accelerates code synthesis, standard Generative AI models persistently struggle with the "Oracle Problem." They treat test generation as a stateless translation task, lacking the strategic reasoning necessary to navigate multi-layered industrial requirements without hallucinating logic. To bridge this massive "Design Gap," we propose the Agentic-QA Fusion Framework. This stateful, multi-stage architecture transforms automated test generation into an active reasoning ecosystem. Utilizing a specialized "actor-critic" loop comprising Parser, Triage, Architect, Writer, and Auditor agents, the framework autonomously strategizes, generates, and self-heals test scripts. The framework’s cross-industry scalability is empirically evaluated against baseline ML and deterministic LLMs across five complex datasets. This includes baseline commercial platforms (ISIS Travel, Travco Travel, Vantage Towers) and two highly constrained domains: the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) FIRDS system (requiring strict ISO 20022 messaging) and a governmental Job Matching Platform (JMP). By shifting the focus upstream to cognitive requirement analysis, the proposed framework successfully parses deeply nested regulatory logic. It drastically reduces hallucination and redundancy rates to 1.3% and 7.8%, respectively. Furthermore, it guarantees near-perfect syntactic correctness (99.6%) and achieves an industry-leading Mutation Score of 93.4%. Ultimately, while this Agentic approach necessitates higher computational resources to resolve dense enterprise dependencies, it establishes a reliable, zero-touch automation solution vital for modern software quality engineering.
evidence_items.title: AI-Driven Automation of Software Testing to Enhance Software Quality and Enable Agentic AI

evidence_items.summary: The increasing sophistication of quantum computing presents significant challenges to the long-term security, computational efficiency, and operational resilience of digital banking infrastructures that rely on conventional public-key cryptographic algorithms. Although Rivest–Shamir–Adleman (RSA), Elliptic Curve Diffie–Hellman (ECDH), and Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) remain widely established cryptographic mechanisms, their underlying mathematical assumptions are vulnerable to sufficiently powerful quantum computers. Recent standardization of ModuleLattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM), Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA), and Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (SLH-DSA) creates opportunities for quantum-resistant financial transaction security, although computational overhead, transmission requirements, and deployment scalability remain important engineering considerations.
evidence_items.title: Development of the PQC-Benchmark  Algorithm for Evaluating the Performance of  Post-Quantum Cryptographic Algorithms in Digital Banking Transactions Compared with RSA, ECDH, and ECDSA-Based Cryptographic Configurations

evidence_items.summary: While Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit remarkable zero-shot learning capabilities, their deployment in real-time interactive systems is constrained by sparse terminal feedback in long-sequence generation, unstable policy updates, and the computational overhead associated with verbose outputs. To address these challenges, this paper formalizes autoregressive text generation as a discrete-time Markov decision process (MDP) and proposes a latency-aware composite reward optimization framework based on proximal policy optimization (PPO). The core contribution of the proposed method is a multidimensional sequence-level terminal reward that jointly evaluates semantic coherence, lexical diversity, and computational cost. Specifically, a Natural Language Inference (NLI) cross-encoder evaluates the semantic consistency between the input context and the complete generated response, while Shannon entropy and Distinct-N metrics encourage lexical diversity. In addition, a hardware-aware penalty based on generated sequence length and measured inference latency discourages unnecessarily verbose outputs and promotes computationally efficient generation. During policy optimization, the terminal composite reward is propagated through generalized advantage estimation, while a token-wise Kullback–Leibler divergence term regularizes the updated policy against the reference policy. This formulation does not introduce token-level semantic rewards; instead, it combines informative sequence-level evaluation with step-wise policy regularization to improve empirical training stability. We evaluated the proposed framework on a large-scale hybrid corpus containing approximately 320,000 dialogue turns, including real-world English interaction data. Compared with the standard PPO baseline, the proposed method exhibited faster empirical convergence and lower variability in the observed training trajectories. It achieved a BLEU-4 score of 22.87 and a Distinct-2 score of 21.59%, while reducing the average inference latency to 42.8 milliseconds per token under the reported hardware configuration. These results demonstrate the potential of latency-aware composite reward optimization to balance response quality, lexical diversity, and inference efficiency in real-time domain-specific LLM applications.
evidence_items.title: A reinforcement learning-driven framework for real-time human-computer interaction: latency-aware composite reward optimization based on PPO

evidence_items.summary: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among women worldwide. Automated Pap smear image analysis with recent advances in machine and deep learning offer a solution by enabling the development of early detection systems for classifying cervical abnormalities improving accuracy and efficiency and reducing the manual interpretation which is labor-intensive and subject to interobserver variability. This study proposes and evaluates a segmentation free methodologies framework for classifying cervical cancer, using machine learning focusing on deep learning, feature extraction methodology evaluation, and hybrid approaches. The Herlev Pap smear dataset used which contains 917 single cell images distributed across seven diagnostic categories. The framework specifically analyzes the performance of various machine learning classifiers combined with multiple feature extraction techniques, including Haralick and wavelet-packet texture features, autoencoder-learned features, and deep features from a pretrained VGG network. ANOVA is used for texture feature selection, while PCA followed by LDA is used to obtain compact class-discriminative representations from high-dimensional deep features. Six classifiers were evaluated under tiered five-fold cross-validation (CV) across three distinct tasks: multi-class classification, normal versus abnormal classification, and a more specific multi-class classification to differentiate between various cancer types and multiple normal categories. The strongest classification performance on our results demonstrates that hybrid approaches, particularly those integrating autoencoder features with texture descriptors, consistently achieved near-perfect binary classification and reached approximately 99.85%/99.96% test accuracy / F1-score for cancer-class classification using random forest. VGG-based representations also showed stable performance, especially for normal-class classification, reaching approximately 100% accuracy with tree-based classifiers. These findings underscore the value of combining unsupervised feature learning with classical handcrafted interpretable texture features to develop robust and complementary information for Pap smear classification. The proposed framework offers a transparent and computationally efficient alternative to fully end-to-end deep learning pipelines, while acknowledging the need for larger multi-center external validation before clinical deployment.
evidence_items.title: Synergistic fusion of deep and handcrafted features for accurate and robust machine learning based cervical cancer diagnosis

evidence_items.summary: Ensuring the reliability of AI-powered information retrieval systems is critical in high-stakes domains such as first aid. Traditional audit methodologies are often static, manual, and unimodal, failing to address the dynamic, time-sensitive, and multimodal requirements of these applications. To overcome these limitations, we introduce RADAR-FirstAid (Reliability-Aware Dynamic Auditing Framework), a closed-loop auditing pipeline — not a competing information system — for real-time, multimodal, and edge-aware auditing. Its key components include a Dynamic Query Simulator for generating criticality-weighted scenarios, a Multimodal Audit & Fusion Agent for verifying cross-modal consistency, a Differentiable Reliability Evaluator that employs LLM-based judges for automated assessment, and an Edge-Optimization Scheduler for efficient deployment. Applying the framework to a curated dataset of 1, 508 first-aid queries, we conduct a large-scale audit of Google’s AI Overviews (AIO) and Featured Snippets (FS), operated purely as black-box Systems under Audit. The audit reveals substantial reliability gaps: automated consistency scores of \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$\Phi _{cons}=0.68$$\end{document} (FS) and 0.72 (AIO), safety/relevance scores of \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$\Phi _{safe}=0.71$$\end{document} (FS) and 0.76 (AIO), and pronounced weaknesses on safety-critical “Binary” and “How-to” queries and on negative-sentiment queries where cautious tone matters most. Manual annotation on a 200-query subset validates the automated evaluation (Spearman \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$\rho = 0.74$$\end{document}–0.87). Ablation studies confirm the essential role of each pipeline module, and geographical variance is minimal (SD \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$<0.03$$\end{document}). RADAR-FirstAid offers a scalable, automated, and reproducible audit instrument for AI-powered search systems in safety-critical domains.
evidence_items.title: A closed loop multimodal auditing framework for enhancing artificial intelligence reliability in medical emergency response

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Aim: To map publication growth, collaboration, knowledge structure, and thematic change in artificial intelligence (AI) research in primary health care (PHC) and general practice and assess whether attention has expanded from model development to validation, implementation evaluation, and governance. Background: PHC AI research covers risk stratification, screening, diagnostic support, clinical decision support, and workflow optimization. However, publication growth and changing hotspots do not directly indicate clinical implementation or practical value. Methods: Web of Science Core Collection was searched for AI- and PHC-related records published from 1 January 2015 to 19 October 2025. Of 1,481 records, 1,261 articles and review articles were screened using titles, abstracts, and author keywords, Python-developed term lexicons, weighted scoring, and manual adjudication. Records lacking a specific PHC application, focused on public or consumer health, or insufficiently relevant were excluded. The main sample included 1,123 papers for bibliometric, collaboration, thematic, citation, and bibliographic coupling analyses. A supplementary search identified 599 candidates to assess omissions due to terminological variation; 142 remained after 457 exclusions and were added to form a 1,265-paper sensitivity corpus used only for keyword-frequency, co-occurrence, and annual trend reruns. Annual output was assessed for 2015 to 2024; 2025 was retained as an incomplete-year observation but excluded from complete-year comparisons. Findings: Annual output rose from 6 papers in 2015 to 220 in 2024 and increased continuously after 2018. Sensitivity analyses confirmed a stable thematic structure centred on AI, machine learning, PHC, electronic health records, screening and diagnosis, with overall increases in standardized AI- and PHC-term frequencies. Bibliographic coupling identified multiple application settings and model-evaluation topics. Model validation became more common; implementation/workflow remained visible, governance/regulation emerged after 2018, and fairness/bias and explainability were more prominent from 2022 to 2024. These findings indicate broader research attention, but do not demonstrate routine AI use or improved clinical outcomes.
evidence_items.title: Artificial intelligence in primary health care: a focused bibliometric mapping of research trends and changes in thematic attention (2015–2025)

evidence_items.summary: Bacterial and fungal leaf diseases frequently produce overlapping visual symptoms, complicating automated diagnosis and limiting the transferability of models across crops and field conditions. This review systematically evaluates artificial intelligence methods for the morphology-based detection and differentiation of these diseases. Following a PRISMA-based selection process, 95 records published between 2017 and 2026 were identified, of which 59 eligible studies were included. The survey covers the morphological characteristics that distinguish bacterial and fungal diseases, traditional image processing and machine learning approaches, deep learning and generative AI techniques, and publicly available datasets. It also critically compares the performance, advantages, and limitations of existing diagnostic approaches. The findings indicate that deep learning dominates the literature, particularly in fungal disease detection, whereas research on bacterial diseases and generative AI applications remains comparatively limited. Although convolutional and transfer-learning models generally demonstrated strong classification performance, comparisons across studies were constrained by differences in datasets, evaluation protocols, and performance metrics. The principal barriers to practical adoption include morphological overlap between infections, class imbalance, and scarcity of expert-annotated images of bacterial and early-stage diseases, reliance on controlled-background datasets, limited external validation, model complexity, and insufficient interpretability. Future research should prioritize pathogen-balanced multicrop field datasets, standardized reporting and cross-dataset evaluation, multimodal fusion of RGB images with spectral and environmental data, domain adaptation, validated generative augmentation, explainable models, and lightweight edge deployment. By connecting lesion morphology with methodological and dataset evidence, this review provides a structured roadmap for developing robust, interpretable, and field-ready plant disease diagnosis systems.
evidence_items.title: Artificial intelligence methods for morphological analysis and diagnosis of bacterial and fungal leaf diseases

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Objective: In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) and its applications have become a compelling topic in psychiatry. This study aimed to investigate whether the AI chatbot ChatGPT is useful for patient education by evaluating the quality, reliability, and readability of its responses to patient questions about repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS). Methods: Twenty-five frequently asked questions about rTMS were separately queried to ChatGPT-4 with no follow-up questions. Responses were reviewed by three psychiatrists by using the Global Quality Scale (GQS), DISCERN tool, and Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) Benchmark Criteria. Readability was evaluated by the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and the Gunning Fog, Coleman-Liau, and Simple Measure of Gobbledygook Indexes. Results: Overall, the quality of ChatGPT responses was moderate to good, with a mean GQS score of 3.69. The mean DISCERN score was 35.33, which is considered poor, and the JAMA Benchmark Criteria score was 0 for all questions. The mean readability score was high (mean grade level, 10.98). Conclusion: Our results show that ChatGPT responses to patient questions about rTMS are of acceptable quality and usefulness. However, the reliability and accuracy of the responses are limited, and a high reading level is required to understand them. Although ChatGPT can support patient education about rTMS, it should be used with caution and under guidance from healthcare professionals.
evidence_items.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT responses to common questions about rTMS: can ChatGPT support patient education about rTMS?
Explainable and Trust-Oriented Evaluation for Determining Suitable Augmented and Synthetic Data Proportions in IoT Intrusion Detection.

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a computational approach for analysing the complex and heterogeneous data generated across oral cancer diagnosis and management. This narrative review provides an integrated overview of AI applications from early oral lesion detection, computational pathology, prognostic assessment, and precision therapeutics. It describes how machine learning and deep learning process clinical photographs, digitized histopathological images, whole-slide images, radiological examinations, and molecular or clinical data to generate task-specific outputs. The review covers AI-assisted identification of suspicious oral lesions, histopathological detection of oral epithelial dysplasia and oral squamous cell carcinoma, assessment of tumor differentiation, characterization of disease progression, and prediction of treatment response for therapeutic stratification. Particular attention is given to the relationship between the input data, computational task, and clinically relevant output rather than to model architecture alone. Although several studies report high diagnostic performance, much of the current evidence remains based on retrospective datasets and internal validation, while external, multicentre, and prospective evaluations are comparatively limited. Major challenges include dataset quality and representativeness, domain shift, annotation variability, interpretability, and integration into clinical workflows. Future progress will require patient-level evaluation, multicentre validation, multimodal integration, uncertainty-aware prediction, and prospective assessment of clinical utility. This review outlines the evolving role of AI as a potential decision-support framework across the oral cancer care pathway.
evidence_items.title: AI driven oral cancer diagnosis from clinical imaging and computational pathology to precision therapeutics

evidence_items.summary: This systematic literature review (SLR) synthesises recent evidence on artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled Air Traffic Control (ATC) decision-support systems and examines how AI is used to improve operational performance, safety, and resilience in increasingly complex airspace. Research on machine learning, optimisation, and automation has expanded rapidly, but evidence remains fragmented across application areas and validation settings. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020-guided protocol was used to search Scopus and IEEE Xplore for English-language journal articles published from 2021 to 2025. Following screening, full-text eligibility assessment, and final reconciliation of study type, scope, and duplicate records, 30 eligible primary studies (n = 30) were included in the qualitative synthesis. The abstract level reporting completeness appraisal yielded a mean score of 80.28% and a median of 83.33%; 16 of 30 studies (53.33%) scored at least 80%, including six studies (20.00%) that scored at least 90%. These percentages describe reporting completeness rather than algorithmic performance. Because the included studies evaluated different operational tasks, datasets, outcome measures, and validation settings, their performance results were not directly commensurable; combining them into a single pooled model-performance percentage would therefore risk conflating non-equivalent metrics. Performance evidence was instead synthesised comparatively by application area, validation setting, and operational trade-off, so that study level performance was interpreted within the metric and dataset used by each primary study rather than averaged across non-equivalent tasks. Three themes were identified: (1) AI-enabled ATC/Air Traffic Management (ATM) operations, including delay and capacity management, conflict resolution, trajectory prediction, and traffic-pattern analytics; (2) aviation safety, surveillance, and resilience, including unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-related risks, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) interference, sensing, monitoring, and safety assurance; and (3) aviation-connected smart mobility and intelligent transportation systems (ITS), including UAV logistics and related surface-transport applications. Comparative synthesis indicated that prediction methods were increasingly connected to operational decision support, whereas conflict-resolution and resilience approaches continued to rely substantially on simulation, experimental datasets, or bounded validation environments. Overall, the evidence showed increasing operational relevance, but important gaps remained in explainability, real-world validation, human-AI interaction, robustness, and system integration before wider safety-critical ATC deployment.
evidence_items.title: AI-Enabled ATC Decision Support Systems: A Systematic Review Of Trajectory Prediction, Conflict Detection, And Human-AI Teaming In The Loop

evidence_items.summary: This study examines how sustainability communication in luxury retail shapes brand trust and behavioral intentions, focusing on consumers' post-exposure perceptions of information quality and provider type. Building on perceived objectivity and perceived persuasiveness, the study explores how consumers evaluate identical sustainability information attributed to either a human agent or an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot, and how these perceptions influence brand trust, information acceptance intention, and purchase intention. A scenario-based experiment with 346 participants was conducted, and the data were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Perceived objectivity and perceived persuasiveness were positively associated with brand trust, which inturn mediated their relationships with information acceptance intention and purchase intention. The indirect effect of perceived objectivity was significant only under AI communication, suggesting that algorithmic provider cues may strengthen the trust-mediated role of objectivity, whereas perceived persuasiveness remained consistently associated with trust and behavioral intentions across provider types. Subgroup analyses further suggest a conditional pattern: among consumers with lower perceived brand luxury, the links between brand trust and behavioral intentions were stronger under AI communication, whereas no significant provider differences emerged among those with higher perceived brand luxury. As these results derivefrom split-sample multi-group comparisons rather than a formal interaction test, they should be regarded as subgroup-based evidence. These findings extend luxury branding research by showing how AI provider cues shape perceived information quality in sustainability communication and by highlighting the need to align provider strategy with consumers' perceptions of luxury brands.
evidence_items.title: Luxury fashion brands’ AI-powered sustainability chatbot communication: how information qualities and brand luxury perception shape consumer trust and behavior

evidence_items.summary: Malware continues to evolve through obfuscation, packing, polymorphism, and other evasion techniques, challenging traditional detection approaches. Data mining (DM) and machine learning (ML) is become important by the day for identifying malicious software through static characteristics, runtime behaviour, and combinations of both. This review examines 46 selected studies on malware detection using DM and ML, with emphasis on static, dynamic, and hybrid analysis. The selected literature is synthesized according to malware platforms, datasets, feature representations, learning algorithms, reported performance, and methodological limitations. The review indicates that static analysis provides computationally efficient detection based on features such as PE headers, strings, byte sequences, and opcode representations, whereas dynamic analysis provides behavioural information through API calls, system calls, memory traces, and execution activities. Hybrid approaches combine complementary feature sources and have demonstrated promising detection performance across several studies. Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, and ensemble-based approaches are frequently reported, while deep learning approaches are increasingly explored for complex feature representations. However, comparison across studies is constrained by differences in datasets, class distributions, feature engineering procedures, and evaluation protocols. Recurring limitations include small or imbalanced datasets, limited real-world validation, insufficient evaluation against unseen malware, computational overhead, and limited model interpretability. Based on these observations, the review identifies explainable artificial intelligence, transfer learning, lightweight real-time detection, and temporal evaluation as important directions for future research.
evidence_items.title: Malware Analysis Using Data Mining Techniques: A Review of Static, Dynamic and Hybrid Analysis

evidence_items.summary: Brain tumor subregion segmentation from multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is important for glioma diagnosis, treatment planning, and disease monitoring. This study presents a ResNet50-U-Net integrated deep residual framework for segmenting Whole Tumor (WT), Tumor Core (TC), and Enhancing Tumor (ET) regions from multimodal MRI. Four MRI modalities, namely FLAIR, T1, T1ce, and T2, are combined as a four-channel input to transform the multimodal input compatible with the ResNet50 encoder. The proposed ResNet50-U-Net was compared with CNN and U-Net baselines using Dice Similarity Coefficient, Intersection over Union, HD95, precision, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, parameter count, model size, and training time. The primary experiments were conducted on 368 labelled BraTS2020 cases using a patient-wise split of 257 training, 55 validation, and 56 independent test cases. Over tumor slice selection, 17,053 for training, 3,573 for validation, and 3,706 for testing were obtained. The proposed ResNet50-U-Net achieved the highest Dice scores for WT and ET segmentation, with values of 0.9100 and 0.8151, respectively, while the CNN achieved the highest TC Dice score of 0.7915. Cross-dataset generalization was evaluated on 95 independent BraTS-Africa glioma cases using an independently retrained instance of the same ResNet50-U-Net architecture, without fine-tuning or external threshold optimization. It is observed that patient-level Dice scores of 0.8592 ± 0.1674, 0.7387 ± 0.2500, and 0.6990 ± 0.2310 were obtained for WT, TC, and ET, respectively. These findings indicate that the proposed framework provides strong WT and ET segmentation on BraTS2020 and retains meaningful segmentation capability on an unseen external cohort, although cross-dataset robustness varies across tumor subregions.
evidence_items.title: ResNet50-U-Net integrated deep residual framework for brain tumor subregion segmentation using multimodal MRI

evidence_items.summary: Artificial data synthesis is a valuable tool for overcoming the challenges of collecting large datasets, particularly in the medical domain where privacy concerns are significant. However, synthesising complex biomedical signals remains difficult due to their intricate morphologies and subject-specific constraints. While GANs have shown promise, existing methods have largely been limited to short-duration outputs or morphology-centered single-pulse events. In this study, we propose a generative framework combining autoencoders and adversarial learning-based disentanglement to enable multi-step, subject-specific biosignal generation with transferable properties, evaluated under a within-recording, segment-level protocol. We evaluate our model on two modalities: Electrocardiogram (ECG; 17 subjects) and Photoplethysmogram (PPG; 7 subjects). The model generates continuous ECG sequences of approximately 6 s (two forward recurrent steps beyond the seed segment), with a subset of subjects retaining recognisable waveform structure up to approximately 8 s. It shows similar performance for PPG, suggesting adaptability across periodic biosignal modalities. With recurrent subject-conditional generation demonstrated across both ECG and PPG, and exploratory style-transfer capabilities demonstrated for selected ECG subjects, the proposed framework serves as a proof of concept for multi-step sequential biosignal generation.
evidence_items.title: Continuous multi-step ECG and PPG generation through latent disentanglement.

evidence_items.summary: Network intrusion detection systems (IDS) are still a staple of the contemporary cybersecurity infrastructure, but the traditional methods based on fixed signatures and theoretical rule sets are still not able to overcome the high false positive rates, slow detection and a general inability to follow the fast changing tactics used by attacks. These are especially acute in settings where encrypted traffic streams, heterogeneous IoT devices and advanced adversarial interactions that strategically bypass signature-based defenses are present. In this paper, the author presents the Maintainable Adaptive AI (MAI) model, a new two-stage ensemble architecture, which combines gradient boosting (XGBoost) with a lightweight feedforward neural network to provide real-time continuously adaptive intrusion detection. The MAI model also uses dynamic feature selection of the lexical, host-based, traffic-based, and statistical attributes in addition to an incremental learning process directed by the KL-divergence-based drift detection. In contrast to earlier, ad hoc proposals of adaptive IDS, the MAI framework is specifically maintainable by a selective retraining of components that only increases the weight of the neural networks when in standard operation and initiates a complete ensemble recalibration when distribution drift is beyond predefined thresholds. Thorough testing using four different sets of data, which are the Malicious URLs Dataset (651,191 entries), ISCX VPN-NonVPN Traffic Dataset (200,000 samples), TON IoT Dataset (400, 000 samples), and a newly curated Custom Scraped Dataset (cumulative of approximately 200,000 real-world attack logs across open-source threat intelligence feeds) prove precision of 93–96, recall of 92–95 and overall Formal complexity analysis The computational tractability of the model is defined and inference latencies of 1.8 ms per sample with batched computation on a GPU, which can be deployed at network links with throughput as high as 4.3 Gbps. Initial adversarial robustness evaluation shows that the model still achieves more than 83% accuracy with combined URL perturbation attacks, and the competitiveness and even better performance are proved by the comparison to other recent state-of-the-art solutions such as federated boosting algorithms, collaborative SRU networks, and concept-drift-sensitive random forests. The experimental code and model settings are accessible in the public to reproduce and research them at the repository where Data Availability section is provided.
evidence_items.title: Devising maintainable adaptive AI (MAI) model for improved network intrusion detection

evidence_items.summary: Federated edge frameworks assume static pipelines, but real latency comes from ingestion, preprocessing, and aggregation delays. To address this shortcoming in federated edge intelligence, we propose Adaptive Federated Pipeline Optimization (AFPO). The framework jointly optimizes pipeline-stage allocation, federated aggregation, and model compression under dynamic edge conditions. We present a 3-layer architecture (sensing tier, federation tier, inference tier) that uses a Reinforcement Learning-based scheduler to assign pipeline stages based on real-time resource telemetry, a latency-aware aggregation mechanism that reduces the effects of stragglers, and an Adaptive Compression Module that dynamically adapts quantization and pruning based on latency feedback. We demonstrate that this problem is strongly NP-hard and establish that AFPO will converge under non-IID data, time-varying network conditions, and deadline-based straggler dropping. AFPO was evaluated empirically on the CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST image-classification benchmarks. Compared to the baselines of FedAvg and FedProx, which are tailored to training, it cuts down inference latency by 35.7%, decreases the communication overhead by 40.6%, and boosts classification accuracy by 5.08 percentage points. This accuracy advantage is specific to those baselines. Against inference-optimized baselines reconstructed in the same simulation environment, AFPO attains the lowest latency and communication cost but slightly lower accuracy (0.896 versus 0.905–0.910). It therefore trades a small amount of accuracy for improved latency and communication efficiency. The RL-based scheduler is trained using a policy-gradient approach. The latency and communication-efficiency enhancements over rule-based, resource-aware, partition-based, and early-exit scheduling are statistically significant across eight random seeds with 95% confidence intervals. Significance applies to three non-IID severities, two network regimes and a second synthetic workload profile. For the image-classification workloads evaluated here, AFPO offers an effective approach to latency-aware federated edge intelligence in Internet of Things and autonomous systems applications.
evidence_items.title: Adaptive federated data pipeline optimization for low-latency AI inference in distributed edge computing environments

evidence_items.summary: Brain–computer interfaces promise restored communication and movement, yet accuracy achieved under development rarely survives new sessions, users, tasks, or hardware. Generalization, not peak performance, determines clinical scalability. Here we examine generalizable neural decoding from development to deployment, organized by the domain held out at evaluation, target-data access, adaptation strategy, and the clinical conditions under which performance persists, identifying benchmarking standards, prospective validation, and hardware-algorithm co-design as prerequisites for durable benefit.
evidence_items.title: Generalizable neural decoding for clinically scalable brain-computer interfaces

evidence_items.summary:
Background
Safe vacuum-assisted vaginal birth depends on appropriate case selection, accurate cup placement, controlled traction, recognition of technical difficulty, and timely abandonment of an unsuccessful attempt. Simulation-based education can improve procedural performance, but evidence that vacuum-specific simulation changes patient-level clinical practice remains limited.


Objective
This study aims to estimate the change in the occurrence of cup detachment (known as "pop off") following implementation of a standardized simulation-based training program for vacuum-assisted vaginal birth. Cup detachment was designated as the single primary outcome after evaluation of the preintervention cohort but before any postintervention versus preintervention comparative analysis.


Methods
This multicenter quasi-experimental before-and-after study is being conducted in 19 Spanish maternity hospitals participating in the Registro Español de Morbimortalidad Materna y Perinatal. The implemented preintervention observation period ran from November 28, 2024, through February 28, 2026. The training and washout phase was conducted during March and April 2026, followed by postintervention data collection from May through October 2026. Preintervention clinical variables are ascertained retrospectively from medical records, whereas postintervention data collection is prospective. The intervention combines preparatory theoretical material, a 1-hour face-to-face simulation workshop using a PROMPT FLEX obstetric simulator and vacuum devices, checklist-based assessment, supervised practice, feedback, and debriefing. The primary outcome will be analyzed using modified Poisson regression to estimate risk ratios and 95% CIs, accounting for hospital and protocol-defined calendar time trends. Sequential instrumentation and conversion to cesarean birth will be analyzed separately as key secondary clinical outcomes. Ethical approval was granted by the Clinical Research Ethics Committee of Girona (code 2024.070) on August 5, 2024.


Results
This study was funded in November 2024. During the preintervention phase, 1155 cases were recorded in 19 hospitals; 12 were excluded according to the selection criteria, leaving 1143 eligible cases. At the verified July 2026 project update, 144 postintervention cases had been collected. Postintervention data collection is scheduled to close in October 2026; the protocol-defined comparative analysis will be performed after database lock, with publication of the main results planned for summer 2027.


Conclusions
The current analysis plan was fixed before database lock and before any formal comparative postintervention versus preintervention effectiveness analysis. The protocol also defines assessment of contamination, intervention fidelity, secular trends, and the limitations inherent to a nonrandomized before-and-after evaluation.
evidence_items.title: Impact of a Simulation-Based Training Program on Cup Detachment During Vacuum-Assisted Vaginal Birth: Protocol for a Multicenter Quasi-Experimental Before-and-After Study.

evidence_items.summary: Accurate user-position estimation is essential in integrated sensing and communication systems, where sensing accuracy must be balanced against sampling and computational costs. This paper considers two-dimensional localization of a single ground-plane user through a known elevated uniform rectangular array and the multiple signal classification pseudo-spectrum. The proposed Nelder–Mead MUSIC method combines a uniform coarse search with derivative-free simplex refinement, thereby avoiding an exhaustive fine-grid evaluation of the complete search region. Exact Euclidean antenna–user distances and free-space amplitude decay are retained in the steering vector so that the pseudo-spectrum depends on the candidate position rather than only on direction of arrival. A Cramér–Rao bound that accounts for the unknown signal phase and amplitude is derived as a theoretical performance benchmark, and Monte Carlo simulations examine the effects of signal-to-noise ratio, sample count, array elevation, coarse-grid density, and refinement iterations. The numerical results indicate that, under the modeled line-of-sight single-user conditions, the estimator approaches the adopted bound at sufficiently high signal-to-noise ratios for well-conditioned user geometries, while requiring substantially fewer pseudo-spectrum evaluations than a dense exhaustive search.
evidence_items.title: Nelder–Mead enhanced MUSIC algorithm for efficient position estimation in ISAC systems

evidence_items.summary: Policymakers in Sub-Saharan Africa increasingly face decisions regarding the adoption of machine learning methods for inflation forecasting, yet these approaches are rarely benchmarked against simple persistence models. This study constructs a reproducible, annual panel of macroeconomic indicators for eight Sub-Saharan African economies (1972–2024, N = 424) to compare eight forecasting approaches: a naive random-walk benchmark, two linear econometric models (pooled OLS and country fixed effects), three machine learning models (Elastic Net, Random Forest, and XGBoost), and a recurrent neural network (LSTM) evaluated with and without early stopping. Using a chronological train/validation/test split and pairwise Diebold–Mariano tests, we evaluate out-of-sample predictive accuracy. The empirical results indicate that no estimated model statistically outperforms the naive persistence baseline. While Random Forest, XGBoost, Elastic Net, and the early-stopped LSTM show no statistically significant difference from the random walk, traditional linear models and the uncorrected LSTM are significantly dominated by it. Although implementing early stopping substantially improves LSTM performance, it does not yield a competitive advantage over simpler tree-based ensembles. These findings align with the well-documented random-walk puzzle in global inflation forecasting, suggesting that structural breaks, high volatility, and modest sample sizes pose substantial challenges for highly parameterized forecasting architectures. Consequently, these results suggest that regional central banks and finance ministries should maintain simple persistence models as active baselines when evaluating investments in complex forecasting infrastructure. These conclusions are robust to a battery of additional checks: HAC-Newey–West/Harvey–Leybourne–Newbold-corrected and Holm–Bonferroni-adjusted Diebold–Mariano tests, a strictly lagged-only predictor respecification, expanding-window recursive re-estimation, per-country and subperiod decomposition, LSTM input-sequence-length sensitivity analysis, a pooled AR(1) benchmark, a five-seed LSTM replication, and a country-clustered block-bootstrap Diebold–Mariano test.
evidence_items.title: Evaluating machine learning and econometric models for inflation forecasting: evidence from a Sub-Saharan African panel

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Eluxadoline is a US Food and Drug Administration-approved therapy for irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea and has important contraindications that may influence uptake in older adults. Medicare Part D dispensing patterns remain poorly characterized.


OBJECTIVE
This study aimed to characterize national and state-level trends in eluxadoline dispensing and spending in Medicare Part D from 2016-2023, including geographic variation in population-adjusted rates and differences in dispensing intensity by prescriber type.


METHODS
We conducted a retrospective repeated cross-sectional analysis using Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Medicare Part D Prescribers-by Provider and Drug Public Use Files from 2016 to 2023. Utilization was summarized using standardized 30-day fills (primary) and claims (secondary); state intensity was measured as fills per 100,000 Part D utilizers. Geographic concentration and outliers in state rates were assessed using Gini coefficients and median absolute deviation-based outlier detection. Prescriber-type differences in dispensing intensity were evaluated with negative binomial models of claims with National Provider Identifier-clustered standard errors.


RESULTS
The Public Use Files contained 7826 prescriber-year observations from 3866 prescribers. National 30-day fills rose from 4410.9 (2016) to 19,860.2 (2018) and declined to 15,326.0 (2023). Median state rates increased from 7.3 per 100,000 (2016) to 43.7 (2018) and were 27.6-35.9 in 2019-23; California, Texas, New Jersey, New York, and Florida accounted for 39.5% of fills. State utilizer counts correlated with total fills (ρ 0.80-0.89) more than adjusted rates (ρ 0.03-0.34). Geographic concentration remained moderate in 2018-23 (Gini 0.307-0.352), and New Jersey was a recurrent high-rate outlier. Gastroenterologists comprised 41.5-57.4% of prescribers and had higher claim intensity than primary care (incidence rate ratio 1.17, 95% confidence interval 1.13-1.21). Inflation-adjusted cost per standardized fill increased from $1021 to $1414.


CONCLUSIONS
Eluxadoline dispensing in Medicare Part D is geographically concentrated and heterogeneous, with higher intensity among gastroenterologists. These descriptive benchmarks may inform medication-use monitoring, access and coverage evaluation, and future beneficiary-level studies of safety and appropriateness in irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea care.
evidence_items.title: Eluxadoline Utilization in Medicare Part D, 2016-23: National Trends, Geographic Variation, Prescriber-Type Patterns, and Spending.

evidence_items.summary: This study investigated how co-existence between bacterial species affect virulence and antimicrobial resistance of each other. The effects of co-culturing with Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa) on Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) virulence and survival under sub-MIC antibiotic exposure were assessed in vitro using 12 bacterial combinations. These combinations were divided into three groups: standard, co-isolated (from the same patient), and random combinations. The effect of these interactions on pathogenicity was also evaluated using a mouse model. Co-culture significantly enhanced S. aureus survival following exposure to azithromycin (100%), gentamicin (91.7%), cefepime (91.7%) and ciprofloxacin (58.3%). Likewise, biofilm formation and clot lysis activity were significantly enhanced in 83% and 67% mixtures, respectively. Gene expression analysis revealed significant upregulation of icaD and sspA in 100% and 89% of the tested combinations, respectively, compared with mono-culture. Overall, the results demonstrate an interspecies interaction between the two pathogens which increased antimicrobial tolerance and virulence in S. aureus. Consistent with these findings, co-infected mice exhibited higher mortality rates and elevated bacterial counts in lung and liver tissues. Taken together, these findings highlight the effect of polymicrobial interactions in evaluating bacterial pathogenicity and resistance to antimicrobial agents.
evidence_items.title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa modulates Staphylococcus aureus biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance

evidence_items.summary: This deposit contains the model code, the complete parameter set with provenance labels, all numerical outputs, and the scripts required to regenerate every figure and table in the associated manuscript. The work is a physiologically based kinetic (PBK) analysis of the renal exposure window of emodin, an anthraquinone of rhubarb. The model is an eight-compartment, perfusion-limited PBK model with intestinal and hepatic first-pass metabolism, biliary excretion and enterohepatic recirculation, parameterised for mouse, rat and human. No experimental data were generated: the study is entirely computational. The published pharmacokinetic data used for calibration and external validation are cited in the manuscript; the extracted values are recorded in results/validation split.csv. The absorption term was calibrated against four published rat plasma datasets, and the fitted value with all residuals is included. Code is additionally available under the MIT licence (see LICENSE-CODE.txt); data and figures are released under CC BY 4.0.

evidence_items.summary: The growing complexity of production systems demands intelligent maintenance strategies to enhance efficiency and reliability. This study proposes a Reinforcement Learning (RL)–based maintenance decision framework integrated within a digital twin environment for data-driven production management. The proposed approach combines real-time system state monitoring, digital twins, and RL to learn adaptive maintenance policies. A digital twin of the production system is used as a simulation environment where the learning agent evaluates operational actions, including operating, inspecting, calibrating, and performing maintenance. The decision process is guided by key indicators such as predicted production yield and machine health conditions, allowing the agent to balance production performance with maintenance interventions. The framework is demonstrated through an application to an exemplary stage of a battery manufacturing process, where the learned policy aims to control process degradation while maintaining stable production yield. Simulation results indicate that the proposed approach can effectively anticipate degradation and trigger maintenance actions at appropriate times. The study highlights the potential of combining digital twin technology and RL to support intelligent and adaptive maintenance strategies in smart manufacturing systems.
evidence_items.title: Adaptive Maintenance in Intelligent Production Systems via the Synergistic Integration of Digital Twin and Reinforcement Learning

evidence_items.summary: This work addresses sustainable decision-making in multistage Lithium-Ion Battery (LIB) production, focusing on balancing production efficiency with environmental and material considerations. The rapidly growing demand for high-performance LIBs necessitates the simultaneous optimization of yield, energy consumption, and material usage across highly interconnected manufacturing processes, where small variations or defects can propagate nonlinearly and affect downstream quality. Digital twins have emerged as a powerful tool for system-level monitoring, process understanding, and optimization in battery production. By providing high-fidelity virtual representations of cell-level electrochemistry and process-level dynamics, they allow detailed scenario analysis and predictive evaluation of process interventions. However, such high-fidelity simulations are computationally intensive, making them impractical for iterative optimization, adaptive control, or real-time decision-support in large-scale production environments. To overcome these limitations, we propose a surrogate-based framework that leverages Machine Learning (ML) models to emulate the behavior of digital twins with substantially reduced computational cost. The surrogate models are integrated within a multi-objective optimization scheme, enabling rapid exploration of trade-offs between key performance indicators, including production cost, CO₂ emissions, and cell yield. This approach allows for dynamic, data-driven decision-making that can adapt to process variations, minimize resource consumption, and support sustainable production practices. We demonstrate the framework’s potential in capturing the complex interactions across multistage LIB production and its ability to guide process parameter adjustments for optimal outcomes.
evidence_items.title: Surrogate-Based Decision-Making in Sustainable Lithium-ion Battery Production

evidence_items.summary: This package contains the data and code needed to reproduce every table of results in the article “Explaining the Decline of Natural Wealth per Capita: A Three-Pillar ESG Analysis of the World Bank Wealth Accounts” (Sustainability, MDPI) and its Supplementary Materials. All results are built from a single public source: the bulk download of the World Bank Sovereign ESG Data Portal of 1 May 2026, included unchanged with its SHA-256 checksum. The package also contains the analysis dataset with a codebook, thirty-one Python scripts run in sequence by a master script, the exact package versions, and a verification report that compares every published value with its reproduced counterpart. The scripts cover the construction of the Törnqvist component contributions, the panel estimates for the environmental, social and governance pillars, the decomposition of per capita growth into stock growth and population growth, and the joint specifications on a common sample. They also cover inference after lasso selection, and the clustering and machine learning modules. A full run takes about 45 minutes on two CPU cores, and all random elements are seeded. The code is released under the MIT licence; the data and documentation are released under CC BY 4.0.
evidence_items.title: Replication package for: Explaining the Decline of Natural Wealth per Capita: A Three-Pillar ESG Analysis of the World Bank Wealth Accounts

evidence_items.summary: Data from a computational experiment on reciprocal instruction updating at an LLM-based eligibility gate. A claim-maker discloses three of five true attributes of a fictional proposal, and an auditor may verify one hidden attribute before accepting or rejecting. Everything is synthetic, so there are no human participants and no personal data. Design: four open-weight model configurations, eight directed pairs, two histories per pair (16 histories), four conditions per history (fixed, claim-maker-only, auditor-only, reciprocal), four adaptation rounds, a 40-record held-out endpoint bank per history, and a fixed-archive audit of 320 paired eligible-case draws. ENGINEERING folders come from the preparation phase and are not part of any reported estimate. The "sealed" files were hidden from policy generation and selection during collection and are released after the study ended. raw collection/ ledger.sqlite: authoritative collection ledger

Pipeline Executor — runs the selected pipeline on .h5ad data through method-specific MCP servers, generating a server with an LLM when a method is not registered. evidence_items.summary: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly changing how lessons are planned and teaching materials are prepared. For teacher education this creates both an opportunity and a risk: future teachers may use GenAI to strengthen their pedagogical design skills, or they may rely on it uncritically. This article proposes a methodical model for developing the professional competence of future teachers through innovative technologies, with GenAI-supported lesson design as its core instrument. The model consists of four interconnected blocks: target, content, procedural-technological and evaluative-reflective. Its central procedure is a cycle of “generate – critique – adapt – teach – reflect”, in which future teachers use a GenAI tool to draft a lesson plan, critically evaluate it against curriculum standards and learner needs, adapt it, conduct a microteaching session and reflect on the results. The article describes the stages of implementation in a pedagogical university course, the diagnostic tools for each component of professional competence, and the design of a pedagogical experiment at Bukhara International University. The model shows how innovative technologies can be turned from isolated tools into a systematic means of developing professional competence.
evidence_items.title: IMPROVING THE METHODOLOGY FOR DEVELOPING FUTURE TEACHERS' PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCE THROUGH GENERATIVE AI-SUPPORTED LESSON DESIGN: A METHODICAL MODEL

evidence_items.summary: Agentic AI systems pursue goals through multi-step planning, tool use, memory, and adaptive action, creating governance challenges that differ from those associated with conventional predictive or generative AI. This study systematically reviews governance evidence relevant to agentic AI in Africa and develops an Ubuntu-informed conceptual framework. Following PRISMA 2020, 91 records published from 2019 to April 2026 were analysed through quantitative content analysis and abductive thematic synthesis. The corpus comprises 12 agentic-AI-specific records, 3 agentic-adjacent records, and 76 broader AI-governance records used as contextual evidence. Five literature-derived gaps were identified: accountability across autonomous action chains, infrastructure-aware oversight, bias and representational harm, policy fragmentation, and community exclusion. These findings inform five proposed governance elements: communal impact assessment, collective consent and participation, infrastructure-contingent oversight, African dataset and bias auditing, and communal accountability. The framework is a literature-derived conceptual proposition, not an empirically validated governance instrument, and requires future case-study, expert-panel, and comparative policy testing.
evidence_items.title: Governing Agentic AI in Africa: A Systematic Literature Review of Ethical Challenges, Framework Gaps, and Ubuntu-Informed Governance Solutions

evidence_items.summary: Background: Difficult laparoscopic cholecystectomy carries prolonged operative time, conversion, and morbidity; preoperative identification of high-risk patients aids planning and counselling. Aims/Objectives: To determine the clinical, pathological, and radiological parameters that predict difficult laparoscopic cholecystectomy and to identify independent predictors. Methodology: This prospective observational study enrolled 100 patients undergoing elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic cholelithiasis. Preoperative clinical, biochemical, and ultrasonographic parameters were recorded and correlated with an operationally defined difficult procedure. Associations were assessed using the chi-square test, Fisher exact test, and independent t-test, followed by multivariable logistic regression. Results: A difficult procedure occurred in 26 (26.0%) patients. Significant predictors were gallbladder wall thickening greater than 3 millimetres (13/26, 50.0% versus 8/74, 10.8%; odds ratio 7.82; p<0.001), positive Murphy sign (11/26, 42.3% versus 2/74, 2.7%; p<0.001), prior hospitalisation (12/26, 46.2% versus 4/74, 5.4%; p<0.001), two or more previous attacks (16/26, 61.5% versus 16/74, 21.6%; p<0.001), raised alkaline phosphatase (10/26, 38.5%; p=0.002), and leucocytosis (11/26, 42.3%; p=0.009). Wall thickening remained an independent predictor (adjusted odds ratio 4.62; p=0.021). Conversion to open surgery was required in 2 (2.0%) patients. Conclusions: Gallbladder wall thickening, inflammatory clinical signs, and recurrent biliary disease reliably predict operative difficulty and permit preoperative risk stratification.
evidence_items.title: Evaluation of Clinicopathological and Radiological Parameters in Predicting the Difficulty of Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy

evidence_items.summary: This study proposes an exploratory computational architecture for investigating AI safety and proactive dialogue. Its central theme is the integration of three components: safety-first response generation, the potential parallelization of generation and safety assessment, and interest-guided proactive dialogue. First, the framework proposes temporarily buffering generated responses and evaluating their contextual consistency and potential safety risks before authorizing external release. Second, it explores the possibility of overlapping response generation and safety assessment in time, with the aim of investigating the relationship between safety review and computational efficiency. Third, it proposes inferring conversational interests from previously authorized and transmitted dialogue and using these estimates to inform subsequent responses and proactive questions. Every newly generated response remains subject to safety assessment, and explicit user instructions take precedence over inferred interests. The methodology focuses on separating and coordinating computational processes, structuring response-release authorization, estimating and updating conversational interest weights, and defining empirical evaluation criteria for safety, response quality, latency, computational cost, and the usefulness of proactive questions. This work presents an exploratory conceptual framework and does not claim that the proposed architecture or its potential benefits have been empirically validated. The practical efficiency of parallel processing, the reliability of safety assessment, the accuracy of interest inference, and the appropriateness of proactive questions remain open research questions requiring further theoretical analysis and experimental evaluation

evidence_items.summary: Highlights of the Study This study developed a bioactive electrospun wound dressing by incorporating naringin, a naturally derived flavonoid with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, into poly(ε-caprolactone)/gelatin (PCL/Gel) fibrous mats. Dressings containing 1.5%, 3%, and 6% (w/w) naringin were systematically evaluated for their morphology, wettability, mechanical properties, water uptake, water vapor transmission, sustained drug release, fibroblast response, and in vivo healing of full-thickness excisional wounds. The results identified the 6% naringin-loaded formulation as the most effective dressing for promoting wound regeneration. Key findings: 🟢 Electrospun dressing fabrication: Naringin-loaded PCL/Gel fibrous mats containing 1.5%, 3%, and 6% (w/w) naringin were successfully fabricated by electrospinning a 1:1 PCL/gelatin polymer blend. 🟢 Fibrous morphology: All formulations exhibited randomly oriented, non-woven porous fibrous structures. The average fiber diameters were 0.82 ± 0.46 μm, 2.79 ± 0.92 μm, and 0.89 ± 0.64 μm for the 1.5%, 3%, and 6% naringin formulations, respectively. 🟢 Improved wettability: Increasing naringin concentration progressively reduced the water contact angle from 74.07 ± 0.40° for PCL/Gel/Nar1.5% to 72.23 ± 0.49° for PCL/Gel/Nar3% and 70.80 ± 0.70° for PCL/Gel/Nar6%, indicating enhanced surface wettability. 🟢 Sustained naringin release: All three electrospun dressings provided controlled and sustained release of naringin for at least one week, supporting their potential as localized bioactive delivery systems for wound treatment. 🟢 Diffusion-controlled release: The release profiles followed the Korsmeyer–Peppas model with n values of 0.35, 0.30, and 0.25 for the 1.5%, 3%, and 6% naringin dressings, respectively, indicating predominantly Fickian diffusion-controlled release.

evidence_items.summary: This narrative review examines large language model (LLM) assistance with archaeological literature, code, metadata, and transcription, together with the ethical, legal, and governance conditions on its use. I propose a Zotero Model Context Protocol (MCP) citation-review sequence that records the publication version, source evidence, provisional assessment, and review status. A small case study tests source reading with sixty constructed claims about ten randomly selected papers cited in this manuscript. Ten model-and-reasoning configurations assessed the claims against my human reference judgments. Exact label agreement ranged from 80.0% to 100.0%, with nine configurations matching at least 58 of sixty labels. One evaluator reported the correct source values but selected the wrong label; a matching label could also accompany an inadequate page locator. The study used a controlled PDF interface, one human reviewer, and one run per configuration, and did not test the full Zotero workflow. I recommend establishing permission to process research materials and checking outputs against inspectable evidence. LLM-supplied citations require human source review; citations selected through the author’s own reading can receive an LLM audit, with human follow-up on disagreements, unresolved support, and proposed changes.

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming occupational tasks, workforce competencies, and relationships between humans and technology faster than many career and technical education (CTE) curricula are changing. This theoretical article introduces the Adaptive CTE Renewal Framework to address the growing mismatch between legacy curriculum and AI-transformed work. Drawing on human capital theory, sociotechnical systems theory, institutional theory and path dependence, and adult/workforce learning theory, the framework conceptualizes curriculum renewal across five interacting dimensions: occupational transformation, curriculum currency, faculty capability alignment, program architecture, and external alignment. Six leadership tests are proposed for evaluating whether courses should be retained, revised, integrated, replaced, or retired. The article argues that conventional periodic curriculum review is increasingly inadequate under conditions of continuous technological disruption and proposes continuous curriculum intelligence as an alternative institutional paradigm. Ultimately, CTE relevance depends on institutions' capacity to continuously align curriculum, faculty expertise, program structures, stakeholder evidence, and workforce competencies with evolving occupational realities.
evidence_items.title: When Legacy Curriculum Meets Artificial Intelligence

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence workloads and cloud services require increasingly sophisticated resource allocation, yet conventional scheduling policies may optimize utilization or response time without explicitly accounting for energy consumption and carbon intensity. This paper proposes a Green Artificial Intelligence framework for intelligent resource management that combines workload prediction, energy-aware optimization, service-level constraints, and runtime feedback. The framework estimates near-term demand from system telemetry and selects resource allocations that balance performance, energy use, and operational cost. A carbon-aware objective can incorporate time-varying grid carbon intensity where trustworthy data are available. The proposed evaluation uses trace-driven experiments and a reproducible comparison against static allocation, utilization-based autoscaling, and energy-unaware scheduling. Key measures include energy per completed task, average and tail latency, SLA violation rate, resource utilization, and estimated carbon emissions. A public cloud workload trace and a documented power-measurement model are recommended for implementation in Python. Because no implementation, trace processing, or experiments have been executed for this manuscript, all quantitative results are left pending.

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by the public and healthcare professionals for clinical reasoning. However, they were developed as general-purpose language models rather than dedicated clinical decision-support tools, and their performance in real-world acute heart failure (AHF) management remains insufficiently evaluated. We compared four contemporary AI models with physician decision-making. Methods This single-center retrospective observational study incorporated a cross-sectional AI evaluation of consecutive patients treated at Sotiria General Hospital between July and November 2025, excluding acute coronary syndrome. ChatGPT, ChatGPT Plus, DeepSeek, and an ESC guideline-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) model independently assessed identical standardized cases. Recommendations were compared with physician decisions on diagnosis, treatment, guideline-directed medical therapy, timing, and prognosis using Cohen’s kappa, McNemar’s test, Cochran’s Q, Wilcoxon signed-rank testing, and multivariable logistic regression. Results Diagnostic performance differed significantly across systems (Cochran’s Q=8.477, P=0.037). In the balanced diagnostic cohort, ChatGPT Plus achieved the highest HF accuracy (accuracy 86.5%; sensitivity 87.0%, specificity 86.0%), followed by RAG (accuracy 77.5%), ChatGPT (accuracy 77.0%), and DeepSeek (accuracy 69.0%). For HF within the top three differential diagnoses, sensitivity was 90.0–97.0%; specificity was 70.0% for ChatGPT Plus, 68.0% for RAG, 19.0% for DeepSeek, and 15.0% for ChatGPT. Physician agreement was highest for guideline-directed therapies, with greater variability in prognosis and escalation of care. RAG more closely matched physician therapeutic timing but did not consistently outperform general-purpose models.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence Versus Physician Decision-Making in Acute Heart Failure: A Comparative Evaluation of Four Contemporary AI Systems
