evidence_items.summary: Abstract Patients increasingly form expectations about plastic surgery from social media and other online sources, and artificial intelligence (AI) now functions both as a tool for analyzing that content and as a source of the content itself. This review maps original empirical studies that applied an AI or computational method beyond conventional statistical analysis to social media, online reviews, public digital images, surveys, or crowdsourced data in plastic surgery while reporting an outcome related to the perceptions, questions, experiences, or information exposure of patients or the public. Twenty-six studies published between 2019 and 2026 met inclusion criteria, 19 (73%) of them since 2024. Facial aesthetic surgery was the most represented domain (n = 9; 35%). RealSelf was the most common primary data source (n = 8; 31%), 18 studies (69%) analyzed a single platform, and 18 (69%) analyzed text alone. Sentiment or emotion analysis was the most common computational method (n = 13; 50%), and 16 studies (62%) applied pretrained models or lexicons as released, without training on study data. A human comparator was reported in 10 studies (38%) and external validation in 1 (4%). No study linked patient-generated digital data to a validated patient-reported outcome measure or evaluated these data for surgical education. Work at this intersection is expanding rapidly but remains descriptive, single-platform, and largely unvalidated.
evidence_items.title: Emerging Artificial Intelligence: A New Digital Age Across The Aesthetic Landscape

evidence_items.summary: Industry 4.0 integrates cyber–physical systems, industrial Internet of Things technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and real-time analytics to improve manufacturing performance. However, small- and medium-scale manufacturing facilities frequently face fragmented automation, reactive maintenance, and limited integration between production data and operational decision-making. This study developed and experimentally evaluated an AI-enabled Digital Twin (DT) framework for optimizing a multi-station mechanical manufacturing system in Bangladesh. The manufacturing cell comprised six interconnected stations: raw-material inspection and sorting, automated loading and orientation, CNC machining, drilling and cutting, AI-assisted quality inspection, and automated storage and dispatch. A synchronized DT represented machine states, production flow, queue formation, operating parameters, energy consumption, tool condition, vibration, temperature, and quality outcomes. An AI layer supported anomaly detection and cycle-time prediction, while a multi-objective optimization mechanism balanced throughput and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) against cycle time, energy consumption, defect rate, and unplanned downtime. Three operating configurations were evaluated: conventional programmable logic controller (PLC)-based operation, DT-assisted operation, and DT–AI optimization. During the six-hour production period, the DT–AI configuration increased throughput from 338 to 405 parts, reduced average cycle time from 63.9 to 53.3 s/part, and increased OEE from 67.6% to 84.6%. Energy consumption decreased from 54.8 to 47.6 kWh, the defect rate declined from 5.9% to 2.6%, and unplanned downtime decreased from 38.4 to 17.9 min. The anomaly classifier achieved an accuracy of 94.6%, while the cycle-time prediction model achieved a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.94.
evidence_items.title: Digital Twin-Driven Optimization of Mechanical Manufacturing Systems Using Artificial Intelligence

evidence_items.summary: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent, non-apoptotic form of regulated cell death that is driven by lipid peroxidation. In the past decade, it has emerged as a core pathogenic mechanism in a wide range of human diseases, such as neurodegenerative disorders, cardiovascular disease, cancer, and notably, reproductive dysfunction. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms underlying ferroptosis with a specific focus on the System Xc⁻–GSH–GPX4 axis, iron metabolism, lipid peroxidation, and the regulatory roles of key modulators such as Nrf2, ACSL4, and CISD2. This review also explores the physiological roles of ferroptosis in development, tissue homeostasis, and immune regulation, as well as its pathological contributions to obesity, diabetes mellitus, atherosclerosis, neurodegeneration, stroke, cancer, infectious diseases, and reproductive disorders. A substantial part of this review discusses the role of ferroptosis in the pathogenesis of reproductive disorders, such as male reproductive pathologies, including varicocele, testicular ischemia–reperfusion, cryptorchidism, oligospermia, erectile dysfunction, and testicular cancer, and female pathologies like primary ovarian insufficiency, polycystic ovary syndrome, endometriosis, ovarian cancer, and pre-eclampsia. Moreover, the interplay between ferroptosis and immune dysfunction in reproductive tract infections was highlighted. Furthermore, we evaluated current biomarkers, emerging therapeutic strategies, and key translational challenges, highlighting the promise of ferroptosis-modulating agents for novel diagnostic and therapeutic interventions in reproductive medicine and beyond.
evidence_items.title: Ferroptosis in health and disease

evidence_items.summary: The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the influence of perfusion pressure in postmortem computed tomography angiography (PMCTA) on the visualisation of the coronary arteries. Coronary artery disease is a frequent cause of sudden cardiac death, and PMCTA is used alongside autopsy to assess the coronary arteries, including bypass grafts and stents. Reliable opacification of the coronary arteries is required to identify stenoses and acute occlusions and to assess their contribution to the mechanism of death. However, contrast distribution in PMCTA varies between cases, and perfusion-related artefacts can limit interpretation. Perfusion pressure is one parameter that can be controlled. An important step in this direction has been the recent demonstration that perfusion pressure can be continuously monitored during PMCTA. In this study of twelve postmortem cases (six evaluable), we examined three intravascular pressure groups (40, 60, and 80 mmHg) to assess coronary artery visualisation using a modified contrast agent pump with coupled real-time pressure monitoring and control. In this pilot study, 60 mmHg was the lowest perfusion pressure at which homogeneous coronary opacification with minimal perfusion-related artefacts was observed in all evaluable cases (two cases per pressure group). In one case a perfusion pressure of 80 mmHg depicted the peripheral coronary branches more completely, an observation that requires confirmation in a larger cohort. These findings may contribute to the methodological standardisation of pressure-based PMCTA protocols in forensic practice.
evidence_items.title: Influence of perfusion pressure on image quality in postmortem CT angiography (PMCTA) of coronary arteries: a pilot study.

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Valvular heart disease (VHD) lacks disease-modifying pharmacological therapies. Drug repurposing guided by human genetics may help identify therapeutic opportunities. We aimed to integrate human genetic associations, drug-target information, and clinical evidence to identify repurposing opportunities and prioritise potentially druggable targets across the VHD spectrum.


METHODS
We retrieved VHD-associated genetic variants from the NHGRI-EBI Genome-Wide Association Studies Catalogue and Ensembl, interrogated annotated genes in the Open Targets Platform, and evaluated linked drugs through structured searches of MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov. The study protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251071741).


FINDINGS
We identified 1464 genetic associations corresponding to 844 unique variants and 582 candidate genes. Of these genes, 431 had tractability information and 51 had linked compounds, comprising 388 distinct pharmacological agents, 273 in phase 3 or 4 of clinical development. Drug-linked targets were concentrated in aortic stenosis. Clinical evidence supported therapeutic potential for 14 drugs, with preclinical or mechanistic cardiovascular support for eight additional drugs and adverse cardiovascular signals for four. An exploratory evidence-weighted framework prioritised targets according to genetic-functional evidence, tissue and mechanistic context, and translational tractability.


INTERPRETATION
This genetics-informed evidence synthesis identifies drug-repurposing opportunities and a substantial gap between genetically supported targets and available therapies. The findings provide a hypothesis-generating framework for mechanistic validation and future valve-focused studies.


FUNDING
Limburg Clinical Research Centre of UHasselt, Jessa and ZOL; British Heart Foundation; National Institute for Health and Care Research; UK Research and Innovation; European Research Council; Horizon Europe.

evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, making their susceptibility to jailbreak attacks a critical concern. While prior work has investigated factors affecting model safety, the representational mechanisms underlying variation in jailbreak vulnerability remain poorly understood. This paper introduces a paired response-final divergence framework that characterizes jailbreak-induced representational displacement between same-goal direct and jailbreak responses using hidden states extracted at the final generated token. This framework is applied to 15 open-source LLMs spanning different model families, four alignment strategies, and four attack types. The framework yields three principal findings: First, Difference-in-Means refusal direction suppression showed the largest observed cross-model association with jailbreak amplification among the evaluated representational measures. Second, family-averaged divergence profiles reveal early-onset representational separation in LLM families like Vicuna, while LLaMA models exhibit comparatively lower and more gradual divergence than Vicuna across normalized layer depth. Third, divergence–ΔASR correlation is attack-type-specific: authority framing (r = 0.836) and context manipulation (r = 0.712) produce stronger model-family discrimination, whereas roleplay-based attacks do not. These findings yield a three-profile representational taxonomy: structurally resistant, early-displaced vulnerable, and ceiling-compromised, that provides a representational grounding for the behavioral patterns observed in the evaluated LLM set, with direct implications for safety evaluation design and model selection in high-stakes deployment.
evidence_items.title: Paired response final divergence signatures of jailbreak vulnerability in large language models

evidence_items.summary: Semantic answer caching reduces inference cost by reusing previous responses but may repeatedly serve incorrect answers. Prior research primarily addresses cache matching, verification, and freshness, whereas this study investigates an error-attribution problem: grouping multiple request surfaces under shared source keys can concentrate incorrect answer exposure without proportionally increasing the total number of errors. We evaluated 500 category-balanced MMLU-Pro questions, six instruction-and-format variants, and two instruction-tuned models using fixed multiple-choice predictions. On 400 TEST questions, pairwise answer disagreement was 27.12% for Qwen2.5-3B and 26.90% for Mistral-7B. At a DEV-selected threshold of 0.96, TEST same-question matching achieved 98.59% precision and 99.97% recall. Semantic caching avoided 91.69–92.31% of modeled inference-token cost. Under Zipf demand, mean maximum cumulative wrong reuse per source key rose from 146.8 to 783.2 for Qwen and from 153.3 to 820.1 for Mistral. These approximately fivefold increases partly reflect different cache-key granularities: at the underlying-question level, maxima were 726.0 versus 783.2 and 745.8 versus 820.1, respectively. Net additional wrong labels relative to fresh computation were only 22.1 and 37.55 per 4800 requests. Exposure-aware refresh did not consistently improve accuracy or control-concentrated errors. Reliable cache evaluation should jointly consider correctness, computational cost, error exposure, and aggregation level.
evidence_items.title: When Reuse Repeats Mistakes: Answer Stability and Error Concentration in Large Language Model Semantic Caching

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive molecular subtype of breast cancer that needs to be identified accurately from pathology reports to inform decision-making. Large language models (LLMs) have been reported to show great potential in the automatic extraction of important oncology information from unstructured medical text. Objective We aimed to create and test an LLM-based approach for automatic biomarker extraction and TNBC subtype classification based on breast cancer pathology reports using prompt-engineering techniques. Methods In total, 532 breast cancer pathology reports from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were used. Our approach extracted structured oncology features, such as estrogen receptor status, progesterone receptor status, HER2 status, tumor size, tumor grade, and tumor histology, which were used to identify TNBC. We tested 4 frontier models: GPT-4o mini (released July 18, 2024), GPT-4.1 nano (released April 14, 2025), GPT-5 nano (released August 7, 2025), and Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite. Results The designed framework was able to extract relevant biomarkers and clinicopathological attributes from unstructured pathology reports and allowed for the automated identification of patients with TNBC. Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite showed superior performance in the extraction of clinicopathological attributes. For all models investigated, chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting was shown to outperform other strategies, such as zero-shot and few-shot prompting, for both biomarker extraction and TNBC classification. GPT-4o mini using CoT prompts reported the highest performance for TNBC classification. Conclusions Using prompt-engineering techniques based on LLMs proved to be an efficient method of translating unstructured breast cancer pathology reports into structured clinical information. Moreover, it can be used to accurately identify the TNBC subtype.
evidence_items.title: Large Language Model Framework for Structured Biomarker Extraction and Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Identification From Pathology Reports: Development and Evaluation Study

evidence_items.summary: ABSTRACT The complexity of preparing Merdeka Curriculum teaching modules and prompting constraints in generative artificial intelligence systems provided the background for designing the AIDERA (Artificial Intelligence for Digital Education and Research Advancement) website. This study aimed to evaluate the validity and practicality of the AIDERA application as an AI-assisted tool for preparing Merdeka Curriculum teaching modules relevant to educators' needs. Employing a Research and Development approach framed within the ADDIE model, this development evaluated a zero-prompt interaction mechanism based on parametric forms. Evaluation involved three domain experts and 23 teachers from SMK IPIEMS Surabaya. Data were collected using 1–5 Likert scale questionnaires supplemented with open-ended qualitative feedback fields to gather in-depth suggestions for improvement. Descriptive percentage analysis revealed an expert validation score of 96.67% (highly valid) and user practicality reaching 82.87% (highly practical). Document preparation time efficiency received the highest rating (87.83%), whereas operational independence and usability recorded the lowest achievement (79.13%). Qualitative findings highlighted several technical issues and system refinement notes, including the need for integrative tutorials, optimization of mathematical notation representation, improved responsiveness during simultaneous access, and content template flexibility. Although AIDERA demonstrates strong potential as a supporting tool for module preparation, objective evaluation regarding its impact on learning effectiveness still requires broader further testing. evidence_items.summary: Abstract Rapid advances in cancer genetics and genomics, pathophysiology, diagnostics, and therapeutics have substantially increased the complexity of clinical oncology. Integrating large and diverse data streams into timely, patient‐specific decisions provides a compelling rationale for incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) into cancer care. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) encompasses several classes of models capable of generating new content. This clinically focused review concentrates on GenAI applications based primarily on large language models (LLMs) and vision‐language models (VLMs), as well as emerging agentic systems that use these models to perform coordinated, multistep tasks. LLMs demonstrate substantial medical knowledge, strong performance on oncology‐related assessments, and emerging capabilities in clinical reasoning. Guideline‐ and retrieval‐augmented systems can improve concordance with expert recommendations and interpretation of complex treatment algorithms. LLMs and VLMs have been applied to documentation, patient communication, information extraction and summarization, clinical decision support, and multimodal data synthesis. However, performance varies substantially across tasks and clinical domains, with important limitations including incomplete or outdated information, training‐data bias, automation bias, and confabulation. Agentic AI represents an emerging extension of these technologies in which LLMs or VLMs are incorporated into systems capable of multistep planning, external information retrieval, specialized tool use, and iterative evaluation and refinement. Early oncology applications include evidence synthesis, multimodal clinical decision support, radiology, pathology, surgery, and individualized treatment planning.
evidence_items.title: Generative artificial intelligence in medical oncology: A clinically focused narrative review of large language, vision‐language, and agentic artificial intelligence systems

evidence_items.summary: Objective: To investigate the ability of machine learning to predict the development of cardiovascular complications (heart failure and myocardial infarction) and renal complications (nephropathy and chronic kidney disease) among people with diabetes mellitus and thus detect those at risk earlier. Methodology: Data from the UCI "Diabetes 130-US Hospitals" dataset was used. The number of encounters included in the dataset is more than 100,000. ICD-9 diagnostic codes were utilized to define cardiac and renal complications. Prior to building models, the data was prepared, cleaned, and features were engineered. XGBoost, CatBoost, and Random Forest machine learning models were developed and validated. Also, SHAP and LIME analyses were performed to make the process more transparent. Results: The best-performing algorithm proved to be CatBoost, which obtained an AUC score of 0.94 in case of cardiac complications and 0.79 in case of renal outcomes. The other algorithms performed relatively well as well. The predictors identified with the help of SHAP and LIME analysis turned out to be consistent with some known clinical risk factors. Conclusion: The presented results show that there is a lot of potential in using machine learning techniques for predicting cardiovascular and renal complications among people with diabetes. Machine learning models could help in managing patients proactively and could serve as a tool for doctors' decision making.
evidence_items.title: redictive Modeling for Diabetic Complications Using Artificial Intelligence

evidence_items.summary: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into medical research and publishing represents a transformative shift, offering unprecedented opportunities to streamline workflow efficiency, enhance language clarity, and accelerate scientific dissemination. However, this rapid technological adoption introduces ethical, epistemological, and procedural challenges, including concerns over data fabrication, automated bias, intellectual property infringement, and the erosion of scholarly accountability. A structured analysis of practical applications highlights a clear demarcation between acceptable supplementary uses and strictly prohibited practices. AI tools are unacceptable as co-authors, as authorship demands moral, legal, and scholarly accountability that non-human entities cannot possess. Similarly, generating or modifying clinical images and media using AI remains unacceptable due to the risk of data distortion and misrepresentation. Within the editorial domain, AI systems must not replace peer reviewers or editorial decision-makers. Uploading confidential manuscript content into external AI platforms violates author confidentiality, while automated algorithms lack the contextual judgment and critical reasoning necessary for peer evaluation and final publication decisions. Conversely, AI tools are acceptable for planning the structure of a manuscript, language and grammar corrections, translation, quantitative or qualitative data analysis, and formatting, provided their use is transparently disclosed and critically evaluated by human researchers. Ultimately, the ethical deployment of AI in medical literature hinges on the principle that technology must serve as an auxiliary tool rather than a replacement for human cognition. Human authors, peer reviewers, and journal editors retain full responsibility and accountability for the accuracy, integrity, and scientific validity of published work.
evidence_items.title: Medical publishing in the era of artificial intelligence

evidence_items.summary: Peer review is important in maintaining the quality of scholarly publishing, but the process faces challenges such as shortage of reviewers, delays, inconsistent judgements, and overlooked errors. These challenges have increased the need to consider the appropriate use of artificial intelligence (AI) in peer review. Completely excluding AI or allowing it to function as an autonomous reviewer may not adequately address these problems. A Human–AI Augmented Review model is therefore proposed, in which AI supports clearly defined tasks under human supervision, while reviewers and editors retain responsibility for interpretation, ethical judgement, and editorial decisions. Peer review involves both routine technical checks and complex scholarly evaluation. AI can assist with repetitive and rule-based tasks such as manuscript screening, consistency checking, reviewer identification, and identification of reporting gaps. Human reviewers are still needed to assess methodology, scholarly contribution, and ethical issues. Effective use of AI requires a clear division of responsibilities, verification points within the review process, and governance measures to address bias, hallucinations, confidentiality, and excessive reliance on automation. Careful and limited use of AI can improve efficiency and reduce avoidable errors while maintaining accountability and trust in peer review.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence as an Assistant in Research Evaluation and Peer Review: A Critical Case for Augmentation Without Replacement

evidence_items.summary: The rapid advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) technologies have brought about a radical digital transformation in the delivery, management, and evaluation of healthcare services. In particular, AI-supported applications in the field of global public health offer significant opportunities in many areas, including early diagnosis of diseases, monitoring and prediction of epidemics, provision of personalized healthcare services, development of clinical decision support systems, remote patient monitoring, and efficient management of healthcare resources. This study examines the impacts of AI-supported digital transformation on global public health from a holistic perspective, addressing both the opportunities and challenges presented by digital transformation. For the successful continuation of global digital health transformation, countries must first strengthen their digital health infrastructures and disseminate standards that ensure interoperability among health information systems.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Digital Transformation in Global Public Health

evidence_items.summary: Cities are facing the escalation of pollution, high energy consumption, resource wastage, and consumption patterns that are often not considered in the long term due to the speed of urbanization. Artificial intelligence (AI), as a tool, is increasingly suggested as a method for relieving these pressures, not just as a piece of software, but as a way to run the urban system more efficiently and to make decisions based on data. This paper is a compilation of three works: AI, smart cities, and sustainable living. It builds on the literature review conducted in environmental studies, digital technology, urban governance, and innovation research. The focus is on the use of AI in the transport sector, energy, water supply, waste management, recycling and reuse, e-governance, and consumer behavior. The advantages and disadvantages are evaluated. The case for adoption is complicated by accountability issues if these AI systems go wrong, data privacy and cybersecurity concerns, public trust, unequal access by lower-income groups, and control issues. The paper provides a conceptual approach to the understanding of the use of AI in the support of responsible consumption and sustainable living in smart cities. It portrays AI as a possible means to help make environments cleaner, societies more inclusive, and cities more resilient if it is governed well. The paper concludes with a discussion on future research opportunities and the need for interdisciplinary cooperation in research into AI, sustainability, and smart cities. There is an increasing interest in the development of smart cities, sustainable living, and responsible consumption, which are all related to artificial intelligence. The development of smart cities, sustainable living, and responsible consumption is all on the rise and is related to artificial intelligence.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Smart Cities and Sustainable Consumption: A Theoretical Perspective

evidence_items.summary: The article focuses on the development of a management model for the implementation of artificial intelligence technologies in Ukrainian industry, aimed at ensuring a transition from an enterprise’s technological and organizational readiness to measurable performance outcomes from the use of artificial intelligence. The relevance of the study is determined by the need to accelerate the digital transformation of Ukraine’s industrial sector under conditions of limited financial and human resources, energy-related risks, changes in production chains, and the gradual integration of Ukrainian enterprises into the European digital environment. The study systematizes the key prerequisites that determine an enterprise’s capacity to use artificial intelligence technologies, including the state of technological infrastructure, data quality and accessibility, organizational conditions, staff competencies, economic capabilities, and interaction with the external digital environment. The necessity of distinguishing between the concepts of artificial intelligence readiness, artificial intelligence implementation, and artificial intelligence performance is substantiated. The proposed approach provides not only for the possibility of scaling a solution but also for returning to the stage of use-case selection to adjust the selected scenario or terminate the project in cases of insufficient performance. The practical significance of the obtained results lies in the possibility of applying the proposed management logic by managers and specialists of industrial enterprises when developing a portfolio of digital initiatives, selecting artificial intelligence projects, determining criteria for their piloting, and making decisions on scaling.
evidence_items.title: MANAGEMENT MODEL FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE BASED ON EUROPEAN EXPERIENCE

evidence_items.summary: Arduino-based artificial intelligence (AI) has progressed from basic microcontroller prototyping to local TinyML inference, accelerator-assisted processing, and heterogeneous Linux–microcontroller computing. This critical-integrative review synthesizes selected peer-reviewed experiments and technical documentation to examine deployment architectures, model optimization, validation practices, and resource constraints. The recoverable experimental set contains nine Arduino-specific studies and one transferable microcontroller study; it is illustrative rather than exhaustive. Evidence is strongest in the selected speech, motion, and sensing applications, while the corpus provides less direct experimental support for industrial vision, predictive maintenance, and heterogeneous deployments. The review proposes the Arduino AI Minimum Reporting Framework (AIMRF), an evidence-informed and architecture-aware reporting guideline requiring community testing, together with device-, system-, and lifecycle-level research priorities. Incomplete historical search records and unverified source metrics limit claims about literature-wide prevalence and reporting completeness.
evidence_items.title: Review Article: From TinyML to Heterogeneous Edge Intelligence: A Critical Review of Artificial Intelligence on Arduino-Based Embedded Platforms

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied to the prediction and prevention of sports injuries, yet research in this area remains dispersed across sports science, biomechanics, sports medicine, data science, and engineering, and its intellectual structure has not been systematically mapped. This study conducted a bibliometric analysis of AI research in sports injury prediction and prevention, together with its performance-related applications. Bibliographic records were retrieved from Scopus on 11 July 2026, with no restrictions on the publication year. After screening, 809 documents (694 articles and 115 reviews) published between 1997 and 2027 were analyzed using the Bibliometrix R-package and VOSviewer. Scientific production grew markedly from 2018 onward, increasing from 13 publications in 2018 to 204 by 2025. The corpus was distributed across 371 sources and 3,226 authors and accumulated 13,295 citations. China and the United States were the leading contributors, with closely comparable affiliation-based output. Keyword co-occurrence analysis produced a network of 44 keywords in 6 clusters, in which machine learning and artificial intelligence were the most central terms, closely linked to injury prevention, injury prediction, biomechanics, and wearable sensing. Thematic mapping identified injury prevention, injury risk, and wearable technology as well-developed central themes, while thematic evolution across three periods (1997–2018, 2019–2022, and 2023–2025) indicated a progression from early injury- and sports-specific research through methodological diversification toward applied sports analytics and athlete monitoring. These findings characterize the structure and trajectory of the published literature rather than the demonstrated effectiveness of AI tools in applied sports settings.
evidence_items.title: A bibliometric analysis of artificial intelligence in sports injury prediction and prevention
From TD50 to benchmark dose in nitrosamine risk assessment: evidence from N-Nitrosotrimetazidine carcinogenicity and TGR mutation data

evidence_items.summary: Circadian rhythms represent a key biological dynamic across all kingdoms of life. These cell-autonomous rhythms generated by a gene-regulatory network regulate processes in a time-of-day-specific manner primarily via transcriptional rhythms in a significant fraction of genes. The controlled experiment paradigm can be used to study causal effects at the molecular level using transcriptomic RNA-seq data even in this dynamic scenario. Multiple tools for the analysis of such data, termed differential rhythmicity (DR) analysis, are available but guidance on method choice remains limited. Here, we present a systematic benchmarking study of 12 different methods from 5 packages using a synthetic model of RNA-seq count data that incorporates both empirically estimated mean-dispersion trends and concomitant differential expression changes. By linking method performance to experimental conditions and analytical goals, we provide practical and simple rules of thumb that will help biologists choose appropriate DR methods and extract reliable biological insight from time series RNA-seq data.
evidence_items.title: Different, same, or arrhythmic: an empirically informed benchmark of differential rhythmicity methods

evidence_items.summary: This paper investigates two-dimensional knapsack problems modeled as the Generalized Two-Dimensional Knapsack Problem (G2KP), a variant not previously studied in the literature. The importance of the G2KP lies in its crucial role in designing Branch-Price-and-Cut (BPC) algorithms for the classical Two-Dimensional Bin-Packing Problem. We propose a novel and effective exact solution framework that incorporates both nonnumerically exact and numerically exact algorithms tailored to G2KP. The framework also achieves state-of-the-art performance on the well-known Two-Dimensional Knapsack Problem (with and without item conflicts) and the Two-Dimensional Orthogonal Packing Problem, solving several previously unsolved instances and establishing new benchmark results. These findings highlight the framework’s potential to inspire algorithmic developments for pricing problems in related BPC methods and higher-dimensional packing problems. To support future research, we make the algorithm code, instance data, and detailed results publicly available. History: Accepted by Andrea Lodi, Area Editor for Design & Analysis of Algorithms–Discrete. Funding: This study was supported by the Natural Science Foundation of China [Grants 72271062, 72671084, and 52575565], Science and Technology Projects in Guangzhou [Grant 2024A04J01019], and the Province Natural Science Fund of Guangdong [Grants 2025A1515011297 and 2024A1515010246]. Supplemental Material: The software that supports the findings of this study is available within the paper and its Supplemental Information ( https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/suppl/10.1287/ijoc.2025.1423 ) as well as from the IJOC GitHub software repository ( https://github.com/INFORMSJoC/2025.1423 ). The complete IJOC Software and Data Repository is available at https://informsjoc.github.io/ .
evidence_items.title: Exact Algorithms for Two-Dimensional Knapsack Problems: A Unified Framework with New Benchmark Results

evidence_items.summary: Correlations between objectives are natural in real-world multi-objective optimisation problems. They fundamentally shape the objective landscape and influence the search behaviour of a multi-objective optimiser. Existing continuous multi-objective benchmarks rarely provide the mechanisms to define them explicitly. We present BEACON-M, a continuous many-objective benchmark generator that constructs smooth objectives via Gaussian Process Random Fourier Features and offers explicit user-defined correlations. These correlations can be embedded via two distinct structured correlation matrix formats: single-group and two-group structures. BEACON-M instances are reproducible by construction, and their correlation structures satisfy analytically derived validity constraints. Beyond the generator itself, we analyse and characterise the feasible correlation region and show how correlations reshape dominance structure and objective landscapes. We also provide concrete guidelines for practitioners and algorithm developers to use these problems. To demonstrate the benchmark's use, we run experiments with state-of-the-art multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (dominance, indicator and decomposition-based) with different numbers of decision variables and objectives. Performance depends on the interaction between problem dimensionality (both in the objective and decision spaces) and the correlation structure and strength; no single algorithm is best across all settings, and which method performs best changes systematically with these factors. These findings demonstrate that such problems can inform the development of new algorithms, both Bayesian and evolutionary, and the selection of existing ones when solving a real-world multi-objective optimisation problem.
evidence_items.title: BEACON-M: Continuous Many-Objective Benchmark Problems via Gaussian Process Random Fourier Features with Explicit, Adjustable Correlation

evidence_items.summary: Hallucination-detection systems are usually judged by a single headline metric, computed under a benchmark design that determines what that metric can show. This paper’s contribution is not a detection algorithm — structural coherence scoring is established — but a methodology for measuring exactly what a benchmark proves and what it does not, applied to the SAS Multimetric Tribunal: a seven-module, GPU-free structural classifier combining lexical, entity-mutation, curvature, and logical-inversion signals via a cascading multiplicative penalty (\(\kappa {D} = 0.56\), \(\kappa {R} = 0.15\)). On a stratified 1,800-pair benchmark (HaluEval-Dialogue, HaluEval-QA, TruthfulQA), the tribunal reaches F1 = 98.99% with zero false positives under an A\(\rightarrow\)A identical-text sanity check. We report this figure and then show, using a format-controlled negative (N1) on the same 1,800 IDs, that it measures format asymmetry between source and response rather than hallucination detection. The tribunal flags 1,569 of 1,800 verbatim correct answers presented alone (87.2%), and in HaluEval-QA scores the correct answer as more anomalous than the hallucinated response. Three further findings follow from the same audit. (i) A per-module analysis shows the tribunal’s seven-module core has no content-sensitive module (prior to the optional R3.1 guard): the one module designed to capture semantic divergence (cre isi) gives the same per-ID score whether the response is byte-identical or completely different. (ii) The 87.97-point advantage of multiplicative combination over weighted averaging reported in v4 is an artifact of threshold calibration; under per-scheme thresholds on format-matched negatives, both schemes converge to F1 \(\approx 0.69\) and the multiplicative scheme is worse by AUROC.
evidence_items.title: SAS Multimetric Tribunal: What a Hallucination Benchmark Measures, and What It Does Not A Format-Controlled Audit of Structural Classification

evidence_items.summary: Abstract In pursuit of decarbonization, ammonia has attracted extensive attention as a zero-carbon fuel for marine propulsion. However, unburned ammonia and associated byproducts will alter the lubrication environment of the cylinder liner–piston ring (CL-PR) friction pair and induce abnormal damage, while the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Hence, reciprocating friction tests were conducted under simulated service environments in ammonia marine engines using lubricating oils with varying ammonia contamination forms and concentrations. Based on the integrated evaluation of friction behavior, wear characteristics, lubrication condition, vibration response and mechanical properties, the results indicate that ammonia contamination universally degrades tribological performance, with ammonia solution exerting a more detrimental effect than ammonia gas, and the severity increasing with ammonia concentration. The introduction of ammonia gas primarily weakens oil film integrity and additive anti-wear performance, thereby intensifying mechanical wear. In contrast, the introduction of ammonia solution deteriorates the anti-wear effectiveness of additives, promotes localized starvation and interfacial corrosion, and induces the formation of extensive corrosion products. These effects collectively result in surface softening, stress concentration, and aggravated spalling, leading to a drop of over 40% in elastic modulus and hardness, with an increase of up to 2.7-fold in wear rate compared to fresh oil, ultimately driving the interfacial damage toward a corrosive-wear coupling effect associated with low-strength corrosion layers. These findings reveal the influence of ammonia contamination on the evolution of CL-PR tribological performance, providing a theoretical basis for optimizing lubricant formulations and improving anti-wear design of tribological components in marine ammonia engines.
evidence_items.title: Tribological performance degradation of cylinder liner-piston rings in marine ammonia engines induced by ammonia contamination of the lubricating oil

evidence_items.summary: Abstract This study assessed heavy metal (HM) contamination in the Ravi River, evaluated environmental quality using contamination and bioaccumulation indices, and estimated human health risks from consuming Labeo rohita and Cirrhinus mrigala fish. As part of an environmental monitoring program, samples were collected from five locations (Siphon, Shahdara, M2, Park View, Head Balloki) and analyzed for HMs. Pollution and bioaccumulation indicators, including the geo-accumulation index ( I geo ), contamination factor (CF), enrichment factor (EF), bioconcentration factor (BCF), and bio-sediment-accumulation factors (BSAF), were calculated to evaluate metal transfer pathways within the aquatic ecosystem. Non-carcinogenic (hazard index, HI) and carcinogenic (lifetime cancer risk, LCR) health risks associated with fish consumption were also assessed. Contamination indices showed moderate to high Cd values in both water and sediments, highlighting anthropogenic influence. Meanwhile, Cr and Pb values were in low-to-moderate ranges across sampling locations. The concentration of HMs in fish muscles (mg kg − 1 dry weight) varied across sites and fish species, with ranges of 0.14 to 0.77 for Cd, 0.15 to 0.88 for Cr, and 0.06 to 0.24 for Pb. The non-carcinogenic risk associated with fish consumption remained below the safety threshold (HI < 1). Carcinogenic risks for Cd and Cr were either negligible (LCR < 10 − 6 ) or within an acceptable risk range (10 − 6 to 10 − 4 ). Overall, despite HM contamination, the estimated human-health risk associated with fish consumption remained within acceptable limits. These findings provide valuable information for environmental monitoring, ecological risk assessment, and sustainable management of riverine ecosystems in developing regions.
evidence_items.title: Integrated Assessment of Heavy Metal Contamination in Water, Sediments, and Fish Along the Ravi River, Lahore: Pollution Indicators, Bioaccumulation, and Human Health Risks

evidence_items.summary: Age- and sex-specific body mass index charts are recommended for diagnosing childhood obesity, while waist circumference helps assess cardiometabolic risk. More than 95% of childhood obesity is primary, resulting from excess caloric intake in an obesogenic environment. Secondary obesity should be suspected with early-onset severe obesity, hyperphagia, developmental delay, dysmorphism, short stature, reduced height velocity, delayed puberty, or endocrine features. Primary obesity is usually associated with normal or increased growth velocity, unlike endocrine causes. Evaluation should include detailed history, growth and pubertal assessment, and appropriate investigations. Screening should include glucose, glycosylated hemoglobin, lipid profile, and liver transaminases, especially after 10 years of age or in severe obesity.
evidence_items.title: Evaluation of obesity in children and adolescents

evidence_items.summary: This study examines how tax consultants at ABC Consulting experience Coretax, Indonesia’s Core Tax Administration System, in their professional work. These practitioners were chosen as primary informants because, unlike individual taxpayers who interact with the system occasionally and on their own behalf, they operate it daily on behalf of multiple corporate clients under strict statutory deadlines, making them the most intensive and operationally exposed users of the system. The research follows a descriptive qualitative, interpretivist case-study design and gathers data through in-depth structured interviews. To interpret user experiences in a legally mandated adoption context, the study draws on the Task-Technology Fit (TTF) framework alongside an adapted DeLone and McLean IS Success Model that excludes the intention-to-use dimension. Results show that system quality poses the biggest obstacle, driven by persistent access instability and the lack of a user activity log. Recurring data errors undermine information quality, and the helpdesk is rated as slow and technically underprepared, producing satisfaction scores between 4 and 6.5 on a ten-point scale. A mapping of nine consultant task types reveals that Coretax fully supports only three. In contrast, high-frequency tasks such as mass invoicing and income tax calculation remain poorly served, especially during peak filing periods. The study concludes that Coretax adoption reflects regulatory obligation rather than user satisfaction. Its main contribution is to extend the combined DeLone-McLean and Task-Technology Fit framework to a compulsory, professional-user setting. It shows that system quality functions as a gating condition for task-technology fit when exit is not an option. The study recommends prioritizing server reliability, data accuracy, and functional integration, distinguishing recommendations under the tax authority’s control from those under the consulting firm’s control.
evidence_items.title: EVALUATION OF CORETAX IMPLEMENTATION: A TAX CONSULTANT PERSPECTIVE
RASE for Fire Safety Regulations: A User-Centred Evaluation

evidence_items.summary: Sociologists face the pressing question of how large language model-based technologies can contribute to social theorising. Several social scientists have called for a greater integration of generative AI tools in the social sciences and humanities to speed and scale up the production of social theory. In this article, we adopt a more cautious approach, reflecting on how the adoption of generative AI raises foundational questions about the construction, refinement and evaluation of critical social theory. To make this argument, we create and critically analyse a speculative piece of dystopian sociological fiction. This enables us to explore the values and practices of critical social theory authorship. We argue that authorship must be ‘recentred’, particularly with regard to four key values of authorial practice: (1) standpoint, (2) creativity, (3) pluralism and (4) accountability. In the present moment, the use of generative AI as substitution for authorial practices redefines and potentially threatens authorship in ways that problematises its particular use in generating critical social theory. With regards to standpoint, generative AI technologies run the risk of reproducing an ‘abstract masculinity’ that feminist scholars have long written against. The relational wonder at the heart of social theory creativity is undermined by generative AI use, as is the pluralism of creativity. Generative AI also flattens and overlooks pluralism of voice, as well as dilutes authorial accountability. We sociologists need to defend and rearticulate what we contribute to social theory and its concomitant politics, both in the theories themselves and in the project of social theorising. It is with this in mind that we call for the ‘rebirth’ - that is, the recentralisation - of the human author in critical social theory creation.
evidence_items.title: The rebirth of the author: writing critical social theory in the time of generative AI

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Lymphoma is one of the most prevalent groups of cancers among people aged 15 to 29 years. Increasingly, patients with lymphoma and their caregivers use generative AI systems, supported by large language models (LLMs), to seek cancer-related online health information. Despite the need for plain and clear health information for clinical decision-making, there is a dearth of research on the readability and citation source classification of LLM-supported online health information.


OBJECTIVE
The objective of this study was to assess the reading level and reading ease of lymphoma-related health information using OpenAI's GPT-5.2 model, as well as the citation sourcing of LLM-generated results.


METHODS
Questions were submitted to the LLM through an automated pipeline. The application code was written with Claude and run and hosted on Vercel. Standardized instructions were submitted to the LLM, asking for evidence-based sources with URLs to enable citation analysis. The final dataset included 392 citations garnered from 96 standardized lymphoma-related questions. Readability was assessed using the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and Flesch Reading Ease scores. Citation sources were classified into 9 predefined organization types, and topics included Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma and clinical trials. Differences in readability were tested using linear models fitted to all 392 citations, with standard errors clustered by question. Estimated marginal means (EMMs) were used to summarize model-adjusted readability scores by citation source and topic. When the omnibus test was statistically significant, pairwise comparisons were performed using the Tukey-Kramer adjustment for multiple comparisons.


RESULTS
The Flesch-Kincaid reading levels of the ChatGPT responses by citation source and topic type were determined to be at the college or university level, well above the recommended sixth-grade level. Grade level did not differ by citation source (P=.58). The reading grade level of responses for Hodgkin lymphoma responses was statistically higher than that of clinical trial responses (mean 16.2, SD 3.4 vs 13.6, SD 2.5; P=.005). Flesch Reading Ease scores across source and topic were found to be very difficult at the university graduate academic level and did not differ by source (P=.27) or topic (P=.17).


CONCLUSIONS
Although LLMs frequently produce responses that include cited information, the readability of these outputs may limit accessibility for many patients and caregivers. These findings highlight the need for improved readability standards in AI-generated health information and reinforce that LLM outputs should complement, not replace, professional medical guidance.
evidence_items.title: Readability and Citation Sources of ChatGPT-Generated Responses to Lymphoma-Related Health Questions: Cross-Sectional Study.

evidence_items.summary: Zero-shot visual navigation enables agents to generalize to unseen environments without task-specific training and is core to service robotics, warehouse logistics, and autonomous exploration. Existing approaches are observed to fail to achieve genuine zero-shot generalization: explicit-map methods rely on accurate reconstruction and are sensitive to sensor noise; supervised policies memorize training-scene patterns and degrade under illumination, furniture, and layout shifts; implicit representations offer continuous, differentiable encoding but remain confined to passive reconstruction and lack effective coupling with active decisions. To address this, EBM-Nav is proposed as a zero-shot navigation framework built on an energy-based model. Specifically, a periodic-activation implicit scene encoder is employed to map discrete RGB-D observations into a continuous, differentiable representation supporting arbitrary-resolution spatial queries. An energy function over the observation–action–goal triple is designed to reformulate navigation as gradient descent on an energy landscape. A frozen multimodal large language model is integrated to decompose long-horizon instructions into subgoals and generate candidate directions. A contrastive-divergence learning mechanism is developed with short-step Langevin dynamics to efficiently construct negative samples for training the energy function. Systematic experiments are conducted on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE continuous vision-and-language navigation benchmarks, and it is shown that EBM-Nav significantly outperforms state-of-the-art zero-shot methods in success rate, path efficiency, and navigation accuracy, while providing an interpretable energy-confidence mechanism for decisions. These results verify the energy-landscape zero-shot navigation paradigm, offer a general learning paradigm for embodied intelligence, and extend energy-based models from static perception to sequential decision-making, with methodological implications for service robots and autonomous exploration.
evidence_items.title: EBM-Nav: energy-based model for zero-shot visual navigation via implicit scene representation

evidence_items.summary: We develop an active inference route-planning method for autonomous control of an intelligent agent. The aim is to reconnoiter a geographical area while balancing search and tracking behaviors to maintain a dynamic situational awareness map. To achieve this, we construct an evidence map that reflects our current understanding of the situation, integrating both positive and “negative” sensor observations of possible target objects collected over time, and diffusing the evidence across the map as time progresses. The generative model of active inference uses Dempster-Shafer theory and a Gaussian sensor model to provide input to the agent. The generative process employs a Bayesian approach to update a posterior probability distribution. We calculate the variational free energy across all locations within the sensor radius by assessing the divergence between a pignistic probability distribution of the evidence map and a posterior probability distribution of the target object, including the level of surprisal associated with receiving new observations. Using the variational free energy, we direct the agent’s movement in simulation by taking incremental steps toward a position that minimizes the variational free energy. This approach addresses the challenge of balancing exploration and exploitation, allowing the agent to search large areas while efficiently tracking identified targets. Across 1000 simulation trials, the approach surpasses benchmarks in target observation by an average of 51%–69% across various metrics for a 100-meter sensor radius.
evidence_items.title: Active inference motion control for autonomous persistent surveillance

It can assist in investigating and predicting blood flow dynamics and heat transmission in constricted arteries for thermal therapy, targeted drug delivery, and cardiovascular disease treatment. By replicating the intricate interactions of many nanoparticles with blood, the model also aids in the design and optimization of biomedical devices like stents and artificial organs. The AI technique also makes it possible to make quick, precise, and patient-specific predictions, which helps doctors plan treatments and enhances the efficacy of cardiovascular procedures. evidence_items.summary: Generative AI is now routine in student work, yet instruments measuring the risks attached to that use—over-reliance, misuse, and the reflective practices that guard against them—remain scarce in African higher education. This study reports the initial development and exploratory evaluation of a 23-item Student Susceptibility to AI (SAI) item pool. A cross-sectional survey of 408 students, recruited by convenience sampling at six purposively selected Ghanaian institutions, was analysed using a reverse-coding audit, Principal Axis Factoring with Promax rotation, parallel analysis, false-discovery-rate-corrected comparisons and multivariable regression. No pilot preceded the survey, and one sample informed item evaluation and extraction. Two-thirds of participants (65.7%) reported daily AI use; only 2.0% none. Parallel analysis supported three factors, the fourth eigenvalue falling below the random threshold; both solutions are reported. Internal consistency was acceptable for Over-Reliance, Cognitive Vulnerability and Resilience & Reflection (α = 0.807–0.824) but inadequate for Misuse/Academic Integrity (α = 0.535), and a total composite was unsupported (ECV = 0.373). Use frequency produced the largest group differences of any variable examined, though adjusted predictors explained only 2.7–7.9% of variance. AI use is already near-universal here, so the question is not whether students use these tools but how. Reflective verification practices proved largely independent of the risk dimensions, indicating that susceptibility is not simply a function of use intensity: interventions should target how students interrogate AI output, not how often they consult it. The item pool remains promising but unstable, requiring revision and independent confirmation.
evidence_items.title: Development and exploratory validation of the student susceptibility to artificial intelligence (SAI) index among higher education students in Ghana

evidence_items.summary: Aiming at the bottleneck problems of path explosion and low efficiency of constraint solving faced by dynamic symbolic execution (DSE) in large-scale Web software systems, this paper applies a DSE and test coverage enhancement method combined with artificial intelligence (AI). Firstly, an Actor-Critic dual network model is constructed based on the PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) algorithm. The Actor network outputs the probability distribution of path selection, and the Critic network evaluates the value of path state. Secondly, the path priority sorting strategy is updated through the generalized advantage estimation and pruning mechanism, and the path depth threshold is gradually increased by combining curriculum learning. The key branch priority solving strategy is applied to optimize the efficiency of constraint solving. Finally, after each round of symbolic execution, the coverage increment is used as a reward signal to update the model parameters online and dynamically optimize the path exploration strategy. Experimental results show that this method significantly improves the efficiency of path exploration (the number of paths reaches 225 and 216, respectively) and test coverage (74.9% and 73.4%) on large-scale Web systems, with an average solution success rate of 79.8% and an average vulnerability detection rate of 88%. It has good vulnerability detection capabilities and resource adaptability, and provides an efficient and scalable new paradigm for automated testing of complex systems.
evidence_items.title: Application of dynamic symbolic execution and test coverage enhancement combined with artificial intelligence in large-scale web software systems

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Static biomarkers are increasingly failing to predict outcomes in hepatobiliary cancers, largely due to the profound heterogeneity of the tumor microenvironment. Over the past decade, rapid advances in digital pathology, single-cell profiling, and spatial multi-omics have generated increasingly detailed maps of tumor architecture. Yet, these static snapshots fail to capture the dynamic cellular interactions driving disease progression. Conversely, patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and organ-on-chip models capture functional drug responses but often lack the microenvironmental complexity of the original tumor. In this review, we use the term digital twin to refer to a patient-specific model that is initialized with individual baseline data, linked to measurable biological or clinical readouts, and refined with longitudinal observations. We outline a unified three-layer architecture: A Data Layer (digitizing static atlases), a Physical Layer (engineering high-fidelity PDO avatars using tunable biomaterials), and a Computational Layer (integrating PDOs and patient data). Moreover, we discuss clinical applications, including individualized therapy selection, exploration of resistance mechanisms, and optimization of drug combinations and treatment sequences. Finally, we highlight the major barriers to clinical translation, including limited paired datasets, variable PDO feasibility, and the difficulty of integrating data collected at different time scales. Taken together, these advances may support more individualized and adaptive care in hepatobiliary cancers.
evidence_items.title: Hepatobiliary cancers digital twins: Integrating artificial intelligence-driven multi-omics with organoid dynamics

evidence_items.summary: Recently approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration, 18F-flurpiridaz for positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) enables high-quality assessment of myocardial blood flow (MBF). Its half-life of approximately 110 min supports regional distribution and allows unit-dose delivery. These features make this probe well suited for MBF quantitation and expand access to quantitative cardiac PET at smaller centers. During pharmacologic stress, absolute MBF and myocardial flow reserve provide incremental diagnostic information beyond relative perfusion imaging. These measures have been validated across multiple methods and software platforms. Further study of this tracer under peak exercise may provide clinically relevant assessment of myocardial demand-induced changes in flow. Potential investigational approaches include artificial intelligence (AI)-derived virtual MBF, exercise-adjusted standardized uptake value (SUV) ratio-derived myocardial flow reserve (MFR) surrogate, and direct kinetic modeling during in-scanner ergometry. While conceptually promising, limitations inherent to exercise-based approaches in stress MBF and/or MFR estimation highlight the need for pragmatic research strategies before potential clinical applicability.
evidence_items.title: Evaluation of Myocardial Blood Flow Using 18F-flurpiridaz PET: Established Applications with Pharmacologic Stress and Roadmap for Exercise Stress Implementation

evidence_items.summary: The article provides theoretical and practical substantiation of a methodology for developing the English communicative competence of information technology students based on artificial intelligence (AI) tools. The linguistic, sociolinguistic, discourse, strategic and professional-digital components of communicative competence are specified. A methodological model for integrating AI tools (generative chatbots, speech recognition systems, automated writing evaluation tools) into the learning process is developed, comprising the stages Ta’limda istiqbolli izlanishlar - xalqaro ilmiy-metodik jurnal № 9/2026 ISSN: 3060-527X “diagnosis – modelling – professional simulation – reflection”. A programme of experimental work to verify the effectiveness of the methodology is proposed.
evidence_items.title: SUN’IY INTELLEKT VOSITALARI ASOSIDA IT TALABALARNING INGLIZ TILIDAGI KOMMUNIKATIV KOMPETENSIYASINI RIVOJLANTIRISH METODIKASI

evidence_items.summary: This article examines the linguodidactic foundations for forming and developing the AI competence of both educators and students within the context of the effective use of artificial intelligence technologies in language education. Amidst digital transformation, artificial intelligence-specifically generative language models, chatbots, speech recognition systems, automated assessment tools, and adaptive learning platforms-is becoming a new component of the foreign language teaching and learning process. The article defines an educator's AI competence as a composite of technological knowledge, methodological-pedagogical competence, critical evaluation skills, awareness of ethics and digital security, and the ability to integrate AI tools into language education.
evidence_items.title: PEDAGOG VA TALABANING TIL TA’LIMIDA SUN’IY INTELLEKT TEXNOLOGIYALARIDAN FOYDALANISH KOMPETENTLIGI VA UNING LINGVODIDAKTIK ASOSLARI

evidence_items.summary: This review aims to evaluate the contemporary and evolving role of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging in arrhythmic risk stratification for patients with non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy, specifically focussing on dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and non-dilated left ventricular cardiomyopathy (NDLVC). This review synthesises current data on late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), parametric mapping, strain imaging and artificial intelligence (AI), and contextualises these among emerging genetic risk stratification approaches. Left ventricular ejection fraction has been the cornerstone for guideline-based arrhythmic risk stratification in patients with DCM, despite limited precision. Observational data and meta-analyses have established the presence of replacement fibrosis through LGE-CMR as a powerful independent predictor of ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) and sudden cardiac death. Crucially, the absence of LGE identifies a low-risk cohort. Much recent focus has been on understanding whether more precise characterisation of scar can further enhance arrhythmic risk stratification, for example through scar quantification. Although data exists supporting a potential role for T1 mapping for arrhythmic risk prediction in this cohort, further research is required to support its widespread adoption. Emerging multimodal approaches using artificial intelligence and personalised computational “digital twins” are areas of important interest, offering scope for integration of imaging, electrocardiographic and genomic data layers. Arrhythmic risk stratification in non-ischaemic cardiomyopathies remains challenging despite significant advances. Progressive refinement in precision has accompanied a shift from a restrictive, functional assessment towards an integrated, substrate-driven precision model. CMR represents the cornerstone of this evolution.
evidence_items.title: Arrhythmic Risk Stratification in Non-Ischaemic Cardiomyopathy: The Role of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging

evidence_items.summary: The growing integration of artificial intelligence into governance challenges the conditions under which political authority can be considered legitimate. Algorithmic systems increasingly mediate decisions that shape citizens’ lives, yet their operations frequently bypass human judgment and obscure the justificatory basis of political authority. This article reinterprets John Locke’s political philosophy as a normative framework for assessing algorithmic authority. By reconstructing Locke’s account of reason, equality, consent, and fiduciary trust, it brings his political anthropology into dialogue with contemporary debates on algorithmic accountability and digital constitutionalism. The article argues that AI governance does not merely raise technical or regulatory problems; it threatens the conditions under which citizens can understand, evaluate, and contest the exercise of power. Because many AI systems operate through models that neither officials nor citizens can meaningfully interpret, they generate forms of automated prerogative that weaken the fiduciary relationship between governors and governed. Against this danger, the article advances a Lockean criterion for computational governance: algorithmic authority can be considered legitimate only insofar as it preserves intelligibility, fiduciary accountability, and contestability. Legitimacy cannot be restored through technical adjustment alone; it requires institutional conditions under which power remains publicly intelligible, politically answerable, and open to challenge by those subject to it.
evidence_items.title: From Natural Equality to Constitutional Legitimacy: Locke’s Political Anthropology and Algorithmic Governance

evidence_items.summary: Post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) is a severe complication of traumatic brain injury (TBI). Patients with PTE often experience comorbid neurobehavioral deficits, which further reduce the quality of life and impede the recovery of patients. This review examines behavioral and motor deficits associated with PTE across clinical and preclinical studies, with an emphasis on the need to identify PTE-specific phenotypes that may serve as biomarkers of disease development and progression, as well as distinguish PTE from other forms of epilepsy. Despite growing evidence of post-TBI behavioral and motor abnormalities, their relationship with PTE remains unclear, particularly in preclinical models where direct comparisons are limited between animals that do and do not develop PTE. We further evaluate the application of artificial intelligence (AI) for characterizing these phenotypes throughout post-traumatic epileptogenesis, highlighting its potential to provide automated, objective, and sensitive measures of functional outcomes.
evidence_items.title: Behavioral and motor deficits following traumatic brain injury: implications for post-traumatic epilepsy.

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Low-field magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has regained interest for musculoskeletal imaging due to advances in magnet design, hardware optimization, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based reconstruction, offering improved accessibility, patient comfort, and sustainability.


PURPOSE
This systematic review aimed to explore and summarize the current status of low-field MRI for knee investigations.


STUDY TYPE
Systematic review on MEDLINE, Cinhal, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases. PROSPERO protocol (CRD42024544354).


POPULATION
Approximately 3400 participants (8-89 years) encompassing healthy volunteers, community-based cohorts, and patients with diverse knee pathologies were evaluated. Few studies incorporate phantom experiments.


FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE
This review covered a range of very-low-field (< 0.1 T), conventional low-field (0.1-< 0.29 T), and upper-range low-field (> 0.3 T-0.55 T) with standard, extremity, open, and weight-bearing/standing systems. SE/FSE and GRE sequences, 3D GRE quantitative protocols, and AI-based were used.


ASSESSMENT
Two reviewers independently extracted data on knee protocols, technical parameters, diagnostic performance, and reported advantages and limitations.


STATISTICAL TESTS
Study quality was assessed using appropriate JBI critical appraisal tools. A narrative synthesis and descriptive analysis of the findings from the included studies are provided due to the heterogeneity of the intervention and outcome.


RESULTS
From 3726 records, 31 were included. Low-field MRI demonstrated high diagnostic performance for meniscal and ligamentous injuries but lower sensitivity for early cartilage degeneration. Weight-bearing MRI provided distinct functional information but not direct equivalence to standard MRI. AI-enhanced reconstruction was evaluated in a limited number of single-center, vendor-specific studies and was associated with improved image quality and diagnostic confidence. Important limitations included lower signal-to-noise ratio, reduced spatial resolution, protocol heterogeneity, and limited pathology-validated evidence.


DATA CONCLUSION
Low-field MRI may provide a clinically useful complementary option for selected knee meniscal and ligamentous indications. However, heterogeneous evidence, influenced by field strength, scanner design, sequences, and reference standards, limits claims of equivalence with high-field MRI, particularly for subtle cartilage lesions. Advances in hardware and AI have improved image quality and efficiency; however, evidence is limited and larger standardized multicenter studies are required.


EVIDENCE LEVEL
5.


TECHNICAL EFFICACY
Stage 5.
evidence_items.title: Low-Field MRI for Knee Imaging: Current Insights and Evidence From a Systematic Review.

evidence_items.summary: Cadmium contamination of water poses serious environmental and public-health risks, creating a need for efficient, reusable, and readily recoverable treatment materials. This study developed a magnetic PA6/CNCs–Fe₃O₄ composite from waste polyamide 6 (PA6), cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs), and Fe₃O₄ for Cd(II) removal from aqueous solution. The composite was prepared via in situ co-precipitation and characterised using SEM–EDS, FTIR, XRD, BET, zeta-potential analysis, and VSM. Characterisation confirmed composite formation, retention of the crystalline magnetite phase, mesoporosity, and the presence of Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles, with sufficient magnetic responsiveness for effective separation. Batch experiments evaluated the effects of pH, contact time, initial Cd(II) concentration, adsorbent dosage, and temperature. Under selected conditions of pH 5.0, an initial Cd(II) concentration of 18.97 mg L⁻1, a contact time of 120 min, an adsorbent dosage of 1.0 g L⁻1, and 298 K, the composite achieved an adsorption capacity of 18.62 mg g⁻1 and a removal efficiency of 98.15%. The pseudo-second-order model best described the kinetic data. The linearised Langmuir model yielded a maximum adsorption capacity of 39.68 mg g⁻1, whereas the nonlinear Sips model provided the closest fit on the untransformed scale. Apparent Gibbs free-energy changes ranged from − 21.75 to − 28.38 kJ mol⁻1, indicating favourable adsorption. The composite retained 86.30% removal efficiency after five adsorption–desorption cycles, demonstrating its potential as a reusable, magnetically recoverable adsorbent for Cd(II)-contaminated water.
evidence_items.title: Fabrication and Characterisation of a Waste-Derived Magnetic PA6/CNCs–Fe₃O₄ Composite for Cd(II) Adsorption from Aqueous Solution

evidence_items.summary: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) has become increasingly relevant due to the proliferation of sensing devices and their applications in healthcare, smart environments, and human–machine interaction, yet building reliable systems remains challenging in real-world conditions, particularly when integrating wearable and ambient data in intelligent environments. Recent approaches have explored multimodal learning to fuse heterogeneous sensor data, federated learning to preserve data privacy, and continual learning to incrementally adapt to new activities and contexts. This work presents a focused mini-review on the intersection of Multimodal Learning, Federated Learning, and Continual Learning applied to HAR, emphasizing how these paradigms can complement each other to enable more realistic, scalable, and privacy-preserving systems. The review synthesizes recent advances across these domains, highlighting fusion strategies, personalization methods, incremental learning techniques, and federated protocols. The study surveys state-of-the-art approaches, analyzes common challenges, and categorizes contributions along architectural, algorithmic, and deployment axes. The works reviewed indicate an increasing trend toward adaptive fusion mechanisms, generative replay, local personalization, and communication-efficient optimization as means to mitigate catastrophic forgetting, data heterogeneity, and modality imbalance. Finally, this review outlines research opportunities for multimodal federated continual HAR, identifies unresolved trade-offs among privacy, adaptability, and scalability, and suggests future directions, such as standardized benchmarks and interdisciplinary collaboration, to bridge laboratory settings and real-world deployment.
evidence_items.title: Multimodal continual federated learning for human activity recognition: Trends and challenges

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Indian antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance rarely uses contemporary global frameworks, and Saurashtra is under-represented in the national evidence base. We applied the WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List (BPPL) 2024 and the WHO AWaRe (Access-Watch-Reserve) classification to institutional surveillance data, with national and global benchmarking.


METHODS
Cross-sectional analysis of 2,195 non-duplicate clinical bacterial isolates (May-October 2024) at a 1,200-bed government tertiary care teaching hospital. Susceptibility testing followed CLSI M100-S33 (VITEK 2 Compact; Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion); multi-drug resistance (MDR) followed Magiorakos criteria. Isolates were assigned to BPPL 2024 tiers by resistant phenotype, and agent-level resistance was grouped by AWaRe 2023 category. MDR correlates were explored by multivariable logistic regression. The isolate was the unit of analysis; proportions describe cultured isolates, not infections or patients.


RESULTS
Isolates meeting Critical-priority phenotypes numbered 1,192 (54.3% of the isolate pool): third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales (n = 1,086; 49.5%; ceftriaxone resistance 78% in E. coli and 61% in K. pneumoniae) and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (n = 106; 4.8%). High-priority phenotypes accounted for at most 228 isolates (10.4%). Within the Access group, Enterobacterales resistance was high to ampicillin (89.7% in E. coli) and amoxicillin/clavulanic acid (77-83%) but lower to gentamicin (22-33%); Watch-group fluoroquinolone resistance was 47-73%. Meropenem resistance in E. coli (1%) and K. pneumoniae (7%) was markedly lower than ICMR AMRSN 2023 national estimates (40% and 54%). MDR was present in 58.6% of isolates and was independently associated with ICU admission, age >60 years, tracheal-aspirate specimens, and surgical-department admission.


CONCLUSIONS
Reading isolate-level surveillance data through the BPPL 2024 and AWaRe frameworks adds a priority- and stewardship-oriented layer to the conventional antibiogram. These proportions describe cultured isolates, not the frequency of resistant infection in patients. The low Enterobacterales carbapenem resistance relative to national benchmarks warrants multi-center, consumption-linked confirmation.
evidence_items.title: Recasting Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Through Contemporary Analytical Frameworks: An Integrated Analysis Using the WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List 2024 and AWaRe Classification in a Tertiary Care Hospital of Saurashtra, Western India.
