evidence_items.summary: Anthracyclines remain indispensable anticancer drugs, but their use is limited by dose-dependent cardiotoxicity involving topoisomerase IIβ (TOP2B)-mediated DNA damage in cardiomyocytes. To identify pharmacological features associated with TOP2-directed cardioprotection, we comparatively evaluated a chemically diverse panel of synthetic compounds, repurposed agents and natural products previously reported to modulate TOP2 activity, using dexrazoxane as the reference cardioprotectant. Recombinant human TOP2A and TOP2B inhibition was assessed by kDNA decatenation. Primary neonatal rat cardiomyocytes were pretreated with test compounds for 3 h and co-exposed to daunorubicin (DAU; 1.2 µM) for 3 h, followed by a 45-h drug-free period. TOP2 immunoreactivity was assessed after 24 h of compound exposure and DAU-induced γH2AX after 30-min pretreatment followed by 90-min DAU exposure. Effects on DAU antiproliferative activity were examined in HL-60 cells during 72-h exposure to 19 nM DAU. Dexrazoxane showed protective activity across the investigated endpoints. BNS-22 inhibited TOP2A and TOP2B with similar potency (IC₅₀ ≈ 2 µM for both isoforms) and produced the strongest protection among the experimental compounds, reducing DAU-induced LDH release by 55% at 10 µM, together with a 90% reduction in TOP2 immunoreactivity and 99.97% attenuation of DAU-induced γH2AX. BNS-22 did not attenuate DAU-induced antiproliferative activity in HL-60 cells. Resveratrol and suramin also provided significant protection at higher concentrations. Across this structurally diverse panel, biochemical TOP2 inhibition alone did not predict cardioprotection. Instead, protection was associated with a broader favourable cellular profile comprising low intrinsic toxicity, attenuation of anthracycline-induced DNA damage and, for the most effective compounds, reduced TOP2 immunoreactivity.
evidence_items.title: Pharmacological correlates of topoisomerase II-directed protection against anthracycline-induced DNA damage and cardiotoxicity: a comparative evaluation of catalytic topoisomerase II inhibitors.

evidence_items.summary: Background Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) might reduce tobacco and alcohol use. We synthesised evidence from randomised controlled trials (RCTs) on smoking and alcohol outcomes, including secondary outcomes reported in trials conducted for other clinical purposes. Methods We searched MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, Web of Science, CENTRAL, PubMed, and registries for RCTs comparing GLP-1RAs with placebo from inception to August 18, 2026. Smoking and alcohol outcomes were synthesised using random-effects meta-analyses. We assessed risk of bias (RoB) with RoB-2, and certainty of evidence with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Findings Fourteen trials involving 1149 participants were included; 13 contributed to meta-analyses. Across the 14 trials, 8 recruited participants not seeking either tobacco or alcohol treatment. The other 6 recruited treatment-seeking participants: 3 for tobacco and 3 for alcohol. Eight trials reported smoking-related outcomes, 11 reported alcohol outcomes, and 5 reported both. Follow-up ranged from 6 to 60 weeks. All 4 pooled smoking-related estimates favoured GLP-1RAs, although all 95% CIs included no difference and were compatible with increases and decreases in outcomes; e.g., smoking cessation, OR 1.39 (95% CI, 0.77 to 2.53, k=3). Restricting analyses to semaglutide trials indicated a reduction in cigarettes per day (CPD) (SMD=-0.10, 95%CI:-0.16 to -0.04; k=3). Across agents, pooled estimates favoured GLP-1RAs for days without alcohol (SMD=0.35, 95%CI: 0.12 to 0.59, k=3). Pooled estimates of semaglutide-only trials also favoured treatment for alcohol consumption (grams/day; SMD=-0.56, 95%CI:-0.82 to -0.30; k=2), craving (SMD=-0.60, 95%CI:-0.91 to -0.29; k=2), drinks per drinking day (SMD=-0.59, 95%CI:-0.86 to -0.32; k=3), drinks per calendar day (SMD=-0.48, 95%CI:-0.87 to -0.09; k=2) and heavy drinking days (SMD=-0.45, 95%CI:-0.85 to -0.06; k=3), and alcohol-free days (SMD=0.41, 95%CI:0.09 to 0.73; k=2). Two of 41 assessed results were at low RoB, 31 raised some concerns and 8 were at high risk; certainty was moderate for 1 outcome, low for 4 and very low for 8. Interpretation GLP-1RAs may reduce alcohol consumption and CPD, with the clearest evidence for semaglutide. These findings should be contextualised by most evidence being low- to very-low-certainty. Larger trials are needed to establish clinically meaningful benefit and sustained abstinence.
evidence_items.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists (GLP-1RAs) for treatment of tobacco and alcohol dependence: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials

evidence_items.summary: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common pregnancy complication, with an estimated global prevalence of up to 14%. While lifestyle and genetic risk factors for GDM are well documented, the effect of probiotic supplementation on the management of GDM-specifically through the reduction of insulin resistance as measured by the Homeostatic Model Assessment for Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR) index-has not been systematically evaluated. This meta-analysis aimed to quantitatively evaluate the clinical efficacy of probiotic supplementation in reducing the HOMA-IR index in a population of pregnant women with diagnosed GDM who manage the disease without the use of antidiabetic pharmacotherapy (insulin or oral agents), as well as to address the probiotics as an evidence-based, adjunctive therapeutic strategy for a more effective regulation of the metabolic profile during pregnancy. PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane databases were searched for original research articles published up to August 10, 2025, which could potentially evaluate the impact of oral probiotic supplementation to the reduction of the HOMA-IR insulin resistance index in pregnant women with GDM without antidiabetic medication during the current pregnancy. A random-effects model was applied to estimate weighted mean differences (MDs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Four randomized controlled trials comprising 245 women (128 in the probiotic group and 126 in the placebo group) were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in the HOMA-IR levels in the intervention group compared to the control group (weighted MD: -0.51, 95% CI: -0.90 to -0.11, p = 0.01). Significant heterogeneity was observed among the studies (I2 = 61.3%). The administration of probiotics appears to improve insulin sensitivity in women with GDM and may serve as a useful adjunctive therapy.
evidence_items.title: What is the impact of oral probiotic supplementation on the HOMA-IR insulin resistance index in pregnant women with gestational diabetes mellitus without antidiabetic medication during the current pregnancy? A systematic review and meta-analysis
Construction and benchmarking of the AFISMI water-filled CT phantom against the ACR, AAPM and Catphan 600 phantoms using automated image quality analysis with IndoQCT.

evidence_items.summary: Abstract The application of nanotechnology in drug delivery systems has attracted considerable scientific interest, particularly with respect to improving the therapeutic efficacy and safety profiles of pharmacological agents. This review critically examines nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems for the management of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), a chronic systemic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent synovial inflammation, progressive joint destruction, and significant extraarticular sequelae. Conventional pharmacological strategies such as non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), corticosteroids, conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs), and biological disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) provide disease control but are associated with significant adverse effects upon prolonged use, inadequate joint specific drug concentrations, and limited responsiveness in a subset of patients. Nanotechnology offers a compelling therapeutic solution by enabling targeted drug delivery to inflamed synovial tissue, thereby enhancing bioavailability, reducing systemic toxicity, and extending drug half-life. This review discusses diverse nanotechnology platforms, such as liposomes, dendrimers, polymeric nanoparticles, hydrogels, metal, inorganic nanoparticles, nucleic acid-based carriers, and stimuli-responsive nanocarriers evaluated for RA treatment. The evidence underscores the potential of these systems to overcome the limitations of traditional therapies and to facilitate precision therapeutics in RA. The review also addresses existing challenges in nanomedicine translation, such as inter-patient variability, protein corona formation, endosomes (as a barrier), biocompatibility, and the need for rigorous clinical validation, while outlining future directions including exosome mediated delivery, biomimetic nano-carriers, and stimuli-responsive platforms.
evidence_items.title: Nanocarrier based drug delivery for rheumatoid arthritis: Current strategies and future directions

evidence_items.summary: Hospital operational capacity cannot be reliably represented by a single occupancy indicator because it emerges from the interaction of heterogeneous and interdependent resources, including staffed beds, medical equipment, consumables, sterilization processes, and operational delays. This study introduces a dedicated fuzzy Resource Agent designed to continuously assess the internal operational state of hospital resources independently of patient-demand dynamics. By separating resource-capacity assessment from scheduling and demand management, the proposed agent provides an interpretable and reusable capacity representation that can support higher-level coordination within hospital multi-agent systems. The proposed Resource Agent integrates 17 normalized resource indicators through a 47-rule weighted Mamdani inference system complemented by an explicit critical-resource veto that prevents severe shortages from being masked by favorable secondary resources. The framework was evaluated using a reproducible in silico experimental protocol comprising 12 hourly scenarios observed over 720 h: one normal control and 11 degradation, recovery, oscillatory, abrupt, or isolation scenarios. Threshold calibration used 200 independently generated normal-condition trajectories, and comparative evaluation used 1,000 paired Monte Carlo replications. The restricted time-to-alert estimand assigned non-detections the remaining degraded follow-up. Mean restricted time-to-alert was 3.953 h for the Resource Agent and 73.406 h for the deterministic comparator; excluding the influential near-threshold scenario reduced the exploratory mean gap from 69.453 h to approximately 32.46 h. A literature-informed Fuzzy TOPSIS adaptation yielded 38.102 h overall, whereas the median scenario-level TOPSIS-minus-Resource Agent difference was 0.000 h, indicating comparable performance across most scenarios while highlighting the specific contribution of the critical-resource veto during isolated critical failures. No veto-ceiling violations occurred in 10,000 randomized trials, and only four material quasi-monotonicity inversions were observed in 1,000,000 trials. These findings demonstrate the computational behavior and architectural value of the proposed Resource Agent under a reproducible experimental protocol and provide a computational foundation for future validation using real hospital operational data.
evidence_items.title: A fuzzy multi-agent framework for hospital capacity assessment based on a dedicated resource agent

evidence_items.summary:
Objective
To develop a multiplex real-time PCR assay for simultaneous detection of Rhodococcus equi (choE), virulence (vapA), and macrolide-resistance determinants (erm[46], erm[51]), and evaluate their clinical and temporal trends.


Methods
Clinical R equi isolates (n = 229) obtained from the Hagyard Equine Medical Institute laboratory were collected sequentially over a 3-year surveillance period (2021 to 2023) from 14 states and underwent broth microdilution susceptibility testing. A cohort of 214 isolates with high-quality DNA was characterized using quantitative PCR. Geographic distribution, seasonal trends, and genotypic-phenotypic concordance were evaluated.


Results
The multiplex PCR assay demonstrated 100% analytical specificity. The virulence gene vapA was present in 94.4% (202 of 214) of isolates. The macrolide resistance determinant erm(46) was highly prevalent at 62.6% (134 of 214), showing a significant seasonal increase during July to December periods at 76.6% (vs 58.2% in January to June). Crucially, erm(51) was detected in a single isolate (0.5%), representing its first recorded clinical identification in R equi. Unstratified genotypic-phenotypic agreement for macrolides was fair (κ = 0.22 to 0.25). However, stratification by genomic copy number revealed near-perfect concordance (κ ≥ 0.97) exclusively among isolates harboring > 50,000 target copies. Alternative agents (gentamicin, ceftiofur, minocycline, doxycycline) maintained 97% to 100% susceptibility, regardless of erm(46) status.


Conclusions
While erm(46) is widely distributed across R equi-endemic farms, actual phenotypic resistance expression is strongly copy-number dependent. The clinical emergence of erm(51) expands the known resistome of this pathogen.


Clinical Relevance
Incorporating quantitative molecular screening into routine R equi diagnostics provides crucial real-time therapeutic guidance, supporting precision medicine and targeted antimicrobial stewardship on endemic equine farms.
evidence_items.title: erm(46) copy number determines macrolide resistance in Rhodococcus equi.

evidence_items.summary:
STATEMENT OF PROBLEM
The performance of additively manufactured dental resin restorations has been reported to depend on postprocessing, but the combined effects of cleaning duration and surface glazing on mechanical, surface, and optical outcomes remain insufficiently defined.


PURPOSE
The purpose of this in vitro study was to investigate the effects of material composition, cleaning duration, and glazing agents on the flexural strength, surface roughness (Ra), and color stability (ΔE00; CIEDE2000) of 3-dimensionally (3D) printed resin composites.


MATERIAL AND METHODS
Four A2-shade 3D printed resin composites were evaluated. Bar-shaped (25×2×2 mm) and disk-shaped (Ø10×2 mm) specimens were fabricated. Specimens received 1 of 4 cleaning protocols (minimal cleaning [15-second immersion in 96% isopropyl alcohol without ultrasonic cleaning] or 2, 5, or 10 minutes of ultrasonic cleaning) and 1 of 4 surface conditions (nonglazed control, Palaseal, EQUIA Forte Coat, and COAT-IT), yielding 16 groups per material (n=15/group). Flexural strength (3-point bending; International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 10477:2020), surface roughness (atomic force microscopy), and color stability (ΔE00) were assessed. Data were analyzed by 3-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Bonferroni and Dunnett post hoc tests (α=.05).


RESULTS
Material type, cleaning duration, and glazing agent significantly affected all outcomes (P<.001). Two-way interactions were significant for flexural strength (material×cleaning duration and material×glazing agent, P<.001; cleaning duration×glazing agent, P=.027), but the 3-way interaction was not (P=.560). Longer cleaning generally increased flexural strength and increased Ra in nonglazed specimens, whereas glazing reduced Ra and improved color stability (P<.001 for both). Glazing also increased flexural strength (P<.001), with Palaseal best overall.


CONCLUSIONS
The performance of 3D printed restorations depends strongly on postprocessing protocols. Surface glazing enhanced mechanical and esthetic properties, whereas optimal cleaning duration remained material-specific.
evidence_items.title: Influence of postprinting cleaning duration and glazing agents on the mechanical and surface properties of three-dimensionally printed dental resins: An in vitro study.

evidence_items.summary:
Chloride-induced reinforcement corrosion is a major cause of premature deterioration of reinforced concrete bridge elements exposed to cyclic wetting and de-icing agents.

Visual inspection mainly records the propagation stage, whereas water-soluble chloride testing can identify hazardous conditions before widespread cracking and spalling. Chloride content, however, cannot by itself define the operational condition without considering reinforcement depth, moisture, cracking and electrochemical evidence.

To generalize field measurements of water-soluble chlorides in six transportation structures in Kyiv, evaluate spatial variability and develop a practical diagnostic workflow.

The study covered a bridge over the Lybid River and five overpasses near Poliarna Street, Portova Street and the Osokorky, Nyvky and Chernihivska metro stations. Visual inspection, core or local sampling, layer preparation and silver nitrate titration were used. After removing duplicate and missing records, 103 determinations expressed as percent of estimated cement mass were analyzed.

Water-soluble chloride content ranged from 0.01 to 2.00 %, with a median of 0.55 %. Under the adopted limits for non-prestressed reinforcement, 23 results fell within the common range for conditions 1–3, 36 within condition 4, and 44 within condition 5; the corresponding counts for prestressed reinforcement were 19, 13, and 71. Thirty paired surface/deeper measurements confirmed a non-uniform chloride profile.

Results should be interpreted using assessment levels corresponding to operational conditions 1–5, with separate limits for prestressed and non-prestressed reinforcement and samples taken at two levels. Chloride content alone does not distinguish conditions 1–3; the final condition requires visual, electrochemical, and structural evidence.
evidence_items.title: Practical aspects of chloride effects on reinforced concrete transportation structures

evidence_items.summary: Bounded Agentic Distribution Experiments (v0.7.0): A Reproducible Framework for Comparing Agentic Intervention Discovery with Non-Agentic Search This software implements the computational framework and pre-pilot experimental protocol associated with the research manuscript Evaluating the Incremental Value of Agentic Intervention Discovery over Non-Agentic Search in Multi-Actor Distribution Networks . The framework evaluates whether a generative AI agent can identify economically beneficial operational interventions beyond those discovered by budget-matched non-agentic search. Agentic and non-agentic methods operate within the same typed intervention space, access the same simulator information, and are subject to common evaluation budgets. Candidate interventions undergo deterministic verification of encoded structural constraints and, where applicable, stochastic qualification against economic, service, route, and actor-participation criteria. The reference environment represents a stylized print-media distribution network with 420 retailers, 18 baseline delivery vehicles, uncertain demand, allocation decisions, reverse logistics, route constraints, temporary fleet capacity, discontinuous staffing requirements, and sales-contingent remuneration. Its parameters combine industry-informed inputs, documented benchmarks, modeling assumptions, and calibration targets. The environment is intended for controlled computational evaluation rather than empirical representation of the Italian distribution industry. Experimental design Version 0.7.0 implements two frozen intervention-complexity regimes: Low-complexity regime (RL): allocation reweighting only, with a maximum intervention length of one action. Multi-domain coupled regime (RC): allocation, route transfer, temporary fleet, and forecasting interventions, with a maximum intervention length of three actions. Both regimes use a candidate-evaluation budget of 40 simulator calls.

evidence_items.summary: Automated classification of brain tumors from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an active area of research, but comparisons between published methods are challenging because of differences in datasets, classification tasks, and evaluation protocols. This study reviews five approaches to brain tumor analysis and presents a baseline classifier using MobileNetV2 transfer learning. The baseline uses a frozen ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV2 backbone and was trained for eight epochs on 7,200 MRI images across four balanced classes: glioma, meningioma, no tumor, and pituitary tumor. On a stratified held-out set of 1,440 images, the model achieved 93.3% accuracy and a macro F1-score of 0.93. Most classification errors involved confusion between glioma and meningioma. The study also discusses limitations affecting the reliability and interpretation of the results, including the possibility of near-duplicate images across data partitions, the use of the held-out test set for monitoring during training, and the limitations of the preliminary Grad-CAM analysis. The findings position MobileNetV2 transfer learning as a useful baseline rather than a state-of-the-art solution and identify improvements needed for more rigorous evaluation and explainability. Keywords: Brain tumor classification, MRI, deep learning, transfer learning, MobileNetV2, Grad-CAM, literature review.
evidence_items.title: Brain Tumor Classification from MRI Using Transfer Learning: A Comparative Literature Analysis and a MobileNetV2 Baseline with Preliminary Grad-CAM Analysis

evidence_items.summary: PGGB GDI3Δ v1.5: Population-Scale Validation and Reproducibility Software Description This software package provides the experimental workflow, validation tools, and benchmark materials used to evaluate GDI3Δ v1.5 , a carrier-derived indexing approach for exact reconstruction of paths embedded in pangenome graphs. Pangenome graphs represent genetic variation through interconnected sequences, while individual genomes or haplotypes are represented as paths through those graphs. Efficiently storing and retrieving these paths is important for population-scale genomic analysis. GDI3Δ investigates whether information about which paths visit particular graph nodes can also help represent which paths traverse the connections between them. The method predicts transition membership from node-carrier intersections and records corrections wherever those predictions differ from the observed paths. Additional information preserves traversal order, including repeated node occurrences, while periodic checkpoints support local path reconstruction without decoding every preceding step. Purpose and scope The package evaluates GDI3Δ on three real pangenome graph partitions generated using the Pangenome Graph Builder (PGGB) workflow and associated with Human Pangenome Reference Consortium (HPRC) Release 2 data. Together, these datasets contain: 1,395 indexed graph walks 29,415,437 path steps 232 distinct named individuals represented across the partitions Haplotype-labelled paths and reference paths The 1,395 walks are not 1,395 independent biological samples: the partitions share the same underlying population identifiers. The evaluation focuses on whether the indexing representation preserves the original paths exactly, how much storage its components require, and how it supports reconstruction of selected path intervals. Software functionality The experimental workflow provides: Construction and validation of GDI3Δ v1.5 indexes from GFA graph files.

evidence_items.summary: Preservation copy of an article published in International Journal of Science, Technology and Management . Read the full article: https://ioro.org/ijstm/article/705694772108/705694772108 . Organizations increasingly use artificial intelligence (AI) to improve strategic planning, operational efficiency, and sustainability. However, conventional machine learning models often lack transparency, limiting managerial trust, accountability, and the practical adoption of AI-driven decisions. This study proposes an explainable AI (XAI) framework that integrates predictive analytics, interpretable machine learning, and sustainability indicators to support transparent, reliable, and evidence-based decision-making across technological, organizational, and environmental dimensions. The proposed framework combines Random Forest, XGBoost, and Explainable Boosting Machines with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME). Evaluation uses a benchmark dataset containing operational performance, resource consumption, organizational efficiency, and environmental indicators. Comparative experiments assess predictive accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), explanation consistency, decision latency, computational cost, and sustainability performance. Baseline models include Logistic Regression, conventional Random Forest, and XGBoost without explanation mechanisms. Ablation studies examine the individual contributions of interpretability and sustainability-aware optimization. The experimental evaluation is designed to determine whether the proposed framework improves predictive reliability, explanation quality, and sustainability-aware decisions compared with conventional approaches.
evidence_items.title: Explainable AI for Intelligent and Sustainable Decision-Making

evidence_items.summary: The development of abstractive text summarization for low-resource languages is constrained by the limited availability of high-quality datasets. Although Hausa is one of the most widely spoken languages in Africa, resources for developing and evaluating neural summarization models remain limited. This paper introduces Hausa Summarization (HAUSUMM) dataset, a curated dataset for Hausa news summarization comprising 11,482 article-summary pairs collected from four professional Hausa news outlets through an automated web-scraping pipeline. The reference summaries were derived from journalistic lead paragraphs and exhibit moderate phrase-level abstraction, as indicated by extractive-fragment analysis and n-gram novelty. To establish baseline performance, four summarization architectures, Bidirectional and Auto-Regressive Transformer (BART), Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer (T5), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with Attention, and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) with Attention, were evaluated under controlled experimental conditions using Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE) scores, BERT-based Semantic Similarity Score (BERTScore), and Summarization Consistency (SummaC). A human evaluation of the article-summary pairs was also conducted to assess relevance, factual consistency, coherence, fluency, conciseness, and abstractiveness. The results provide baseline evidence for Hausa abstractive summarization and make HAUSUMM available for further research on Hausa summarization.
evidence_items.title: A Hausa abstractive summarization dataset with baseline evaluation

evidence_items.summary: HBB2OBB converts horizontal (axis-aligned) bounding boxes (HBBs) into oriented (rotated) bounding boxes (OBBs) by using existing HBB annotations as prompts for segmentation models from the SAM (Segment Anything Model) family. It targets object detection tasks where objects appear at arbitrary orientations, such as aerial imagery, satellite data, and traffic monitoring, producing oriented boxes that tightly encapsulate non-upright objects without any re-annotation. Beyond conversion, it provides horizontal box detection, evaluation, hyperparameter optimization, an interactive annotation viewer, and annotation format-conversion tools, exposed through both a command-line interface and a Python API. 📖 Documentation: rfonod.github.io/hbb2obb , with a quick start on the bundled sample data, a guide per command, pages on how the conversion works, the confidence score, the metrics and provenance, and a CLI and API reference generated from the code. Why HBB2OBB 🎯 Accurate OBBs from HBBs : prompts SAM-family segmentation models with existing horizontal boxes to fit tight oriented boxes around non-upright objects, with no re-annotation required. 🚗 No HBBs? Detect them : the hbb2obb-detect command runs an Ultralytics detector over the images and writes the horizontal boxes the conversion consumes, confidence column included. 🧩 Model ensemble : combines masks from multiple SAM variants through majority voting for more robust, accurate results. 🛡️ Spatially constrained and safe : region-specific masking and contour refinement keep segmentation inside the object, a mask split by an occluder is fitted back together, and a fallback retains the original HBB when no valid mask is found, counted and reported rather than left to be discovered afterwards.
evidence_items.title: HBB2OBB: Horizontal to Oriented Bounding Box Conversion and Evaluation Tool

evidence_items.summary: Background . Given the frequent relapses of vulvar lichen sclerosus (VLS) and widespread resistance to treatment, the search for new pathogenetically grounded therapeutic options aimed at improving disease course and reducing the frequency of exacerbations is an urgent task of modern clinical medicine. Objective of the study : to evaluate the clinical efficacy of cholecalciferol as a systemic adjuvant immunomodulatory agent in addition to standard therapy with topical corticosteroids in patients with VLS and laboratory-confirmed vitamin D deficiency. Materials and methods . This prospective study included 100 women aged 18 to 70 years with a verified diagnosis of VLS and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels below 30 ng/mL. The control group (n = 50) received standard monotherapy with topical corticosteroids clobetasol propionate 0.05%. The intervention group (n = 50) additionally received oral cholecalciferol at a dose of 10,000 IU/day for 12 weeks, followed by a maintenance dose of 4,000 IU/day. The follow-up period lasted 12 months, during which symptom severity was assessed using a visual analogue scale, and objective tissue changes were recorded. Results . The combined approach demonstrated a statistically significant advantage. Already after four weeks, a markedly faster reduction in visual analogue scale symptom scores was observed in the intervention group. Complete clinical remission was achieved in 42% of patients in the intervention group compared with 18% in the control group. After one year of follow-up, the relapse rate was 12% in the intervention cohort versus 38% in the control group. Objective examination confirmed significantly more active restoration of the elasticity of affected tissues, rapid epithelialization of existing microfissures, and sustained regression of hyperkeratosis under conditions of achieving target vitamin D concentrations. Conclusions .
evidence_items.title: Clinical experience of the use of vitamin D in the complex treatment of vulvar lichen sclerosus

evidence_items.summary: Overview This repository provides the reproducibility materials accompanying the research manuscript From False to Fluent: A Claim-Disjoint Baseline Study and Preregistered Framework for Evaluating Generative-AI Transformation of Health Misinformation . The study investigates the robustness of machine-learning classifiers for health-misinformation detection under Generative-AI-mediated linguistic transformation. It uses two existing health-information datasets, COVID-19 FNIR and an mpox misinformation dataset, to examine whether classification performance remains stable when original health claims are reformulated without intending to change their underlying meaning or veracity. Experimental framework Four experimental conditions are defined: C0: Original health-information text. C1: Neutral rewriting to improve fluency and readability. C2: Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) central-route transformation, emphasising the organisation of existing reasoning and evidence. C3: ELM peripheral-route transformation, modifying rhetorical emphasis and peripheral persuasive cues. The reported computational experiments evaluate four classical classifiers (logistic regression, linear support vector machine, multinomial naïve Bayes and random forest) and five task-trained neural architectures (1D-CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, CNN-LSTM and CNN-BiLSTM). The analyses examine transformation robustness, changes in textual and persuasion-related features, statistical associations with classification errors, transformation-aware mitigation and cross-dataset transfer. The repository also includes supplementary analyses of class-specific error rates and paired source-root bootstrap confidence intervals for the classical classifiers. Repository contents The archive contains Python source code, preprocessing and evaluation workflows, configuration files, reproducibility instructions, frozen aggregate results, integrity-check materials and supplementary statistical outputs.
evidence_items.title: From False to Fluent_ A Claim-Disjoint Baseline Study and Preregistered Framework for Evaluating Generative-AI Transformation of Health Misinformation

evidence_items.summary: This repository provides a complete Rust implementation of the algorithms developed for the paper “A Joint Projector Formulation of Raw-Data Spectral Clustering is ∃R-Complete: Exact Complexity, Grassmann Geometry, and Projector–PALM.” The software implements the proposed Projector–PALM framework for joint representation learning and clustering, including the reduced relaxed-projector formulation and the exact hard-assignment realization. The implementation follows the mathematical formulation of the paper and includes the main computational primitives required by the theory: simplex projections, projector construction, low-rank projector computation, PALM updates, exact hard-assignment projection, sufficient-decrease backtracking, objective and gradient evaluation, hard-partition certification, and theory-validation experiment drivers. The archive also includes Rust implementations of the six spectral-clustering techniques used for comparison: Raw truncated-SVD score clustering Shi–Malik normalized cut Random-walk normalized-Laplacian spectral clustering Ng–Jordan–Weiss normalized spectral clustering RatioCut / unnormalized-Laplacian spectral clustering Dhillon bipartite spectral co-clustering The package contains command-line experiment drivers, NMI and ARI evaluation routines, reproducibility utilities, regression tests, algorithm-to-paper mappings, release metadata, and the theory-directed experiments used to examine projector geometry, hard-partition certification, local convergence, finite assignment identification, and low-rank projector scaling. The implementation is intended primarily as a research and reproducibility artifact accompanying the theoretical work. The benchmark algorithms are included to provide a common Rust implementation of the spectral-clustering comparison suite rather than to redefine or modify their original formulations.
evidence_items.title: Projected PALM for endn to end ETR Spectral Clustering

evidence_items.summary: Abstract:  The uncritical application of legacy statistical machinery to modern Big Health Data has driven a proliferation of clinically unstable and methodologically fragile studies. This review gives an account of the author's extensive research activity over the past year, continuing into the present, encompassing a corpus of seventy-five papers, seventeen of which are fully peer-reviewed and published, aimed at addressing this methodological crisis despite the widespread and defensive resistance encountered within the academic establishment. By outlining a structured progression from the epistemological auditing of medical artificial intelligence and epidemiological consistency validation to structural dataset auditing and exact finite-count stress testing, this overview suggests that the Big Data p-value Paradox can be solved in the medical field. This passes through the necessity of subordinating massive computational scale to biological plausibility and appropriate statistical mechanics to safeguard public health informatics.
evidence_items.title: Rebuilding Big Health Data: An Account of Seventy-Five Studies

evidence_items.summary: Accurate prediction of the in-cylinder pressure trace does not necessarily preserve pressure-derived combustion descriptors. This study uses a synthetic spark-ignition benchmark to examine whether explicit supervision of these descriptors changes surrogate accuracy. Six neural-network variants share a 5382-parameter architecture and training budget, with cumulative supervision of pressure derivatives, apparent heat release, peak descriptors, combustion phasing and gross indicated work. The benchmark comprises 960 operating points divided into training, validation, interpolation and simultaneous speed–load extrapolation sets, plus a closure-shift test with altered combustion and wall-heat-transfer relations. At the specified 1° output resolution, validation-selected A4 reduces interpolation CA50 mean absolute error from 0.0938° to 0.0688° and maximum pressure-rise-rate (MPRR) error from 0.0506 to 0.0303 bar/°, corresponding to improvements of 26.6% and 40.1%. Pressure RMSE increases from 0.0980 to 0.1031 bar, and gross IMEP error increases from 0.0296 to 0.0529 bar. A4 retains a lower MPRR error during speed–load extrapolation, with higher pressure and work errors, while all models deteriorate under the closure shift. The 1° MPRR discretisation discrepancy of 0.01702 bar/° is comparable in magnitude to the 0.0203 bar/° model improvement. These results establish a redistribution of approximation error within the prescribed benchmark. The fixed geometry, nominal fuel and simplified single-zone generator, together with the absence of experimental validation, preclude interpreting the reported gains as demonstrated improvements on real engines.
evidence_items.title: Derivative and Combustion Metric Supervised Cylinder Pressure Surrogates for Spark-Ignition Engines: A Synthetic Benchmark Study

evidence_items.summary: Replication package for the article Unequal Rewards and the Direction of Scientific Work: Evidence from U.S. Public Universities . It contains the code, the estimation data and the documentation needed to reproduce every table, figure and number reported in the article and its online appendix. Study The article links administrative payroll records of tenure-line faculty at 93 U.S. public universities (fiscal years 2004–2026) to their publication records in OpenAlex. For each department it estimates a department-specific pay equation and measures the pay dispersion that the department’s formal ladder (rank, contract basis, seniority) does not explain. This residualized Gini is related to five dimensions of members’ research: productivity, citations, novelty, conventionality and disruption. The analytic sample has 124,056 department-person records, covering 105,050 faculty members in 4,839 departments. Contents README.md : overview, layout, coding of identifiers, environment. HANDOFF FOR AI AGENTS.md : the pipeline end to end (inputs, outputs, run order, checkpoints), with a map from each table, figure and number of the paper to the script and file that produce it. Written for an AI agent or a human reader.  DATA DICTIONARY.md : every column of every data file in 3 analysis/ . 1 data collection/ : code that acquired and parsed the public salary disclosures, plus the department backfill, Wayback supplement (code only). 2 data cleaning and linking/ : code that assembled the salary panel, standardized names, ranks and departments, linked faculty to OpenAlex authors, and computed the work-level measures (code only). 3 analysis/ : the pseudonymised estimation frames and the analysis code (first stage, panel and matching, tables, figures, appendix analyses), with the shipped outputs. run all.sh and notebooks step by step/ : the full analysis as one shell script, and the same pipeline as one Jupyter notebook per script in run order (outputs saved).

Whether elite International Powerlifting Federation (IPF) classic powerlifters are becoming younger and whether this reflects earlier recorded competition or a younger active population is unclear. This study examined temporal patterns in age, performance and recorded intervals to elite performance.
 
 
 
 Population and top-100 analyses covered 2013 to 2025 and Open World Championship podium analyses covered 2013 to 2026. Earlier OpenIPF records informed competition histories. Population-wide age-performance relationships were estimated using locally weighted scatterplot smoothing and profile-cluster bootstrapping. Trends in annual medians were evaluated using Theil-Sen slopes and Kendall tests. Intervals from first recorded eligible competition to first observed elite performance were calculated among profiles with eligible histories.
 
 
 
 
 The performance cohort comprised 431,476 entries from 161,073 profiles. The population-wide curve peaked at 26.0 years (95% confidence interval [CI]: 25.4–26.5). Active-profile median age ranged from 23.5 to 25.0 years and showed no clear trend (0.00 years/year; 95% CI: −0.10 to 0.00; Kendall
 p
  = 0.173). Population median age at first recorded eligible Raw three-lift competition declined slightly (− 0.097 years/year; 95% CI: −0.200 to 0.000; Kendall
 p
  = 0.0085). Among 1,303 yearly top-100 profile-years and 602 podium observations, median age slopes were − 0.20 years/year (95% CI: −0.29 to − 0.10; Kendall
 p
  = 0.002) and − 0.37 years/year (95% CI: −0.50 to − 0.19; Kendall
 p
  = 0.001), respectively. Median IPF Goodlift Points increased by 1.21 (95% CI: 1.08–1.43; Kendall
 p
  < 0.001) and 1.52 points/year (95% CI: 1.33–1.79; Kendall
 p
  < 0.001), respectively. Median age at first recorded eligible Raw or Single ply three-lift competition showed no clear trend among top-100 profiles (0.00 years/year; 95% CI: −0.05 to 0.00; Kendall
 p
  = 0.289) or podium profiles (− 0.05 years/year; 95% CI: −0.22 to 0.00; Kendall
 p
  = 0.121). Raw-only elite histories showed negative first-competition-age trends. Median recorded intervals were 3.58 years for top-100 profiles and 4.72 years for podium profiles, with no clear temporal shortening.
 
 
 
 
 Median age in elite samples declined while performance increased, whereas active-profile median age showed no clear decline. These descriptive findings provide updated age and performance benchmarks without establishing individual peak ages or faster progression to elite performance.

evidence_items.summary: Predicting blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability is essential for central nervous system drug discovery, but traditional descriptor-based methods of predicting BBB permeability lack structural context, and deep learning-based methods struggle with overfitting. We introduce a multimodel framework that integrates both transformer-derived molecular embeddings with physicochemical descriptors using a late-stage ensemble fusion strategy. Trained on both the B3DB and NeuTox data sets and evaluated on the benchmark BBBP, our model showed strong predictive performance, with data set-dependent performance. Feature fusion improved performance relative to embedding-only models in several settings, whereas descriptor-based models achieved comparable or higher performance in some settings. These results suggest that combining learned structural embeddings with chemical descriptors provides complementary predictive information, while the benefit of their integration may depend on the data distribution or classifier used.
evidence_items.title:

by Integrating Deep Learning Representations with Chemical Compound

evidence_items.summary: Amorphous polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for next-generation lithium batteries. They offer improved safety and mechanical stability compared to conventional liquid electrolytes. However, predicting their transport performance remains challenging. Ionic conductivity and diffusivity depend on complex, coupled interactions between polymer structure, chemistry, and ion dynamics. This work leverages machine learning to predict four key transport properties in amorphous polymer electrolytes using a molecular dynamics data set of more than 6,000 polymer electrolyte systems. These are ionic conductivity, bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (TFSI) diffusivity, lithium-ion diffusivity, and polymer diffusivity. To enhance predictive capability and preserve mechanistic interpretability, we engineered chemically and structurally meaningful features from Simplified Molecular-Input Line-Entry System (SMILES) representations. Selected features include elemental composition, functional group densities, polarity descriptors, and polymer flexibility metrics. Three modeling frameworks were trained and evaluated under 5-fold cross-validation, including random forest, gradient boosting, and neural networks. The neural network achieved the highest predictive performance across all four targets and exceeded prior benchmarks on three of them. It also exhibited substantially greater robustness to data partitioning than the tree-based baselines. Feature importance analysis was performed using both impurity-based rankings and Shapley additive explanations. Polymer backbone flexibility, polarity, and ionic environment were found to dominate transport behavior. Directional attribution further identified primary and secondary amines and carboxylate groups as specific negative contributors to lithium-ion mobility. The results of this work demonstrate that chemically informed structural descriptors can effectively predict electrolyte performance while yielding mechanistic insight. This enables accelerated screening and design of high-efficiency polymer electrolytes for future energy storage applications.
evidence_items.title:
Machine Learning
Prediction of Transport Properties
in Amorphous Polymer Electrolytes Using Chemically Informed Structural
Descriptors

evidence_items.summary: Este conjunto de datos recoge información histórica sobre misiones espaciales y eventos de exploración del espacio, obtenida mediante técnicas de web scraping a partir de Wikipedia en español. El dataset contiene 284 registros y 12 variables, con fechas de lanzamiento comprendidas entre 1944 y 2022. Incluye información sobre las misiones, destinos, países, tipos de misión, resultados, fechas de lanzamiento, vehículos lanzadores y observaciones relevantes. La información procede del artículo Anexo espaciales , consultado mediante un programa desarrollado en Python, que utiliza las bibliotecas Requests y BeautifulSoup. Variables incluidas: mision : denominación de la misión o evento. destino : cuerpo celeste, región o destino de la misión. pais : país o entidad participante. tipo mision : modalidad o clasificación de la misión espacial. resultado : estado o resultado de la misión. fecha lanzamiento : fecha de lanzamiento registrada en la Wikipedia. anio lanzamiento : año de lanzamiento de la misión. cohete : vehículo lanzador utilizado. notas : información complementaria. url mision : dirección url de Wikipedia asociada a la misión. url listado : dirección url de la página utilizada como fuente. fecha extraccion : fecha en que se recopilaron los datos. Procedencia: Wikipedia en español. Fecha de extracción: 18 de octubre de 2026. Finalidad: Estudio de la evolución histórica de la actividad espacial para análisis de destinos, períodos, países participantes, tecnologías y resultados. Limitaciones: El conjunto de datos reproduce información de la Wikipedia. Puede contener registros repetidos de misiones que participaron en varios eventos, datos ausentes, clasificaciones inconsistentes.
evidence_items.title: Misiones espaciales y eventos históricos de exploración espacial recopilados de Wikipedia (1944–2022)

evidence_items.summary: We conduct a version-pinned, reproducible forensic audit of the public Einstein Elevator data package (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.15167723) to determine whether it supports validation of quantum sensor certificates. Through an exhaustive cross-file sliding-window correlation search over 44,207,922 comparisons and exact six-decimal rounding checks, we find that all 31 exported sensor channels have a unique best match within the enumerated raw traces under the stated protocol. Residual numerical differences are highly consistent with text-based absolute quantization; the correlation-loss approximation 1 - r ≈ δ² / (24σx²) is diagnostic for this dataset, not a universal proof. We inspect the MATLAB-derived 318-point population series and reconcile it with a 2022 workbook entry only at the level of counts. An archive-wide search of 181 file objects and 1,654 MATLAB metadata fields finds no documented join key linking the 2022 run-indexed population series to the 2017 timestamped traces under the enumerated search protocol. Using Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds and a Charnes-Cooper linearization, we establish that the public archive does not supply the joint observations needed to identify the EKF false-safe risk without additional coupling assumptions; the formal program is illustrative and is not populated with empirical failure/acceptance coefficients because the required linked observations are absent. We frame this as a bounded data-contract limitation for downstream statistical validation, not as a failure of the original experiment.
evidence_items.title: A Reproducible Provenance Audit of the Public Einstein Elevator Data Package: Trace Correspondence, Metadata Linkage, and the Non-Identifiability of Sensor-Certificate Risk from the Public Archive

authors: Raja Sakthi Kumar R, Selva Ganesh L And Ms. Sri Thejas
evidence_items.summary: Abstract Cloud platforms face two separate risks: hostile network activity and silent changes to stored files. This paper describes an ML-driven cloud security system that addresses both within a single workflow. A two- stage long short-term memory (LSTM) network trained on the UNSW-NB15 intrusion dataset labels network records as normal or attack and returns a confidence score. In parallel, every uploaded file is fingerprinted with SHA-256 and anchored on a permissioned Hyperledger Fabric ledger, so that later tampering can be exposed by recomputing the digest and comparing it with the ledger entry. The prototype combines a React.js client and a Node.js/Express.js service layer with AWS S3 for object storage and Firebase for authentication and activity monitoring. Preprocessing covers missing-value handling, categorical encoding, and feature standardization, and yields 42 input features per record. On the official UNSW-NB15 test partition of 82,332 records, the training pipeline reports a final test accuracy of 91.00% . Because the integrity records are kept outside the storage service, file verification does not depend on the provider being trustworthy. Together, the two modules give layered protection in which suspicious traffic is flagged and stored files remain verifiable. Keywords: Cloud Security, Machine Learning, LSTM, UNSW-NB15, Threat Detection, AWS S3, Firebase, Blockchain, Hyperledger Fabric, SHA-256.
evidence_items.title: ML-DRIVEN CLOUD SECURITY SYSTEM WITH BLOCKCHAIN-BASED INTEGRITY VERIFICATION

evidence_items.summary: Python code that reproduces every number, table and figure of the manuscript “A parity frontier between all-electric and hydrocarbon regimes: the required EROI under changing final energy demand” (Benyahia and Ait Hsain, submitted to Ecological Economics), together with the numerical verification of its propositions. The code takes as input the dataset of Aramendia et al. (2024), available at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.25311358. The paper derives, in closed form, the life-cycle EROI that an all-electric supply system, storage and networks included, requires to match hydrocarbons as a function of the growth rate of final energy demand. With 2020 global data, the baseline requirement at 2% annual growth is 5.5.
evidence_items.title: Replication package for "A parity frontier between all-electric and hydrocarbon regimes: the required EROI under changing final energy demand"

evidence_items.summary: 2. ABSTRACT   Background: Telemedicine can support continuity of care for chronic non-communicable diseases (NCDs), but uptake depends on access, skills and service design. Objective: To estimate awareness, willingness and reported use of telemedicine among adults with chronic NCDs, identify correlates of willingness and describe barriers. Methods: In this facility-based cross-sectional study at an Urban Health Training Centre in Karimnagar, Telangana (May–September 2024), adults with an NCD of at least six months were sampled systematically and interviewed with a structured bilingual questionnaire; 400 of 435 invited completed interviews (response 91.95%). Proportions are given with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CI); associations were tested with chi-square tests and logistic regression. Results: Mean age was 51.4 ± 11.2 years and 53.5% were female. Awareness was 64.3% (95% CI 59.4–68.8), willingness 71.5% (66.9–75.7) and use in the past 12 months 28.8% (24.5–33.4), so at least 171 participants (42.8%) were willing non-users. Willingness fell with age (90.3%, 74.7% and 56.2%; p<0.001) and was higher with smartphone/tablet ownership (adjusted odds ratio 4.12; 95% CI 2.55–6.65), higher education (3.42), age under 40 years (2.85), higher income (2.15) and urban residence (1.95). Among 285 non-users, the leading barriers were low digital literacy (38.6%), preference for in-person care (29.1%) and connectivity or cost (16.5%). Conclusion: Willingness substantially exceeded use, indicating an implementation gap linked to skills, device access and service design. Assisted, low-bandwidth hybrid pathways that retain in-person care merit prospective evaluation; findings are single-centre and associational.   3. KEYWORDS   Telemedicine; non-communicable diseases; digital health literacy; patient acceptance; primary health care; India
evidence_items.title: Telemedicine Awareness, Willingness and Use Among Adults with Chronic Non-Communicable Diseases: A Cross-Sectional Study in Karimnagar, Telangana, India

evidence_items.summary: This dataset provides literature-curated annotations of human microtubule-related genes for neuronal and interphase research. Genes are organised into seven overlapping functional domains: structural tubulins and nucleation; lattice organisation and stability; microtubule-end biology and dynamic instability; severing and remodeling; tubulin modifications; motors and transport machinery; and neuronal microtubule coupling. The workbook contains gene identities, functional assignments, mechanistic evidence summaries, recorded experimental context, critical appraisal, evidence categories, inclusion decisions and supporting references. Excluded and unresolved candidate assessments are retained separately. Candidate identification used Gene Ontology and Reactome annotations processed in R, supplemented by targeted literature retrieval. Supporting publications underwent manual appraisal and supervisory checking. The deposit includes the annotation workbook, a detailed methods and data guide, and supporting code with portable CSV tables. The resource is intended to support transparent gene-set selection, transcriptomic interpretation and experimental planning. It synthesises existing evidence and does not report newly discovered genes or new experimental validation.
evidence_items.title: An evidence-curated dataset of human microtubule-related genes supporting neuronal and interphase functions

evidence_items.summary: Light is an essential and often limiting resource for photoautotrophs, especially phytoplankton, composed of different quantities (irradiance) and qualities (wavelengths). Its availability varies on timescales from seconds to decennia, intensified by human-induced perturbations such as increased terrestrial run-off or eutrophication. Phytoplankton possess a comprehensive inventory and diversity of pigments to exploit distinct niches along the vertical light gradient underwater. These light-associated traits add an extra layer of complexity to the already high morphological and biochemical diversity of phytoplankton. The amplitude and frequency of light fluctuations vary predictably by season and day, augmented by stochastic variation on shorter time scales. In combination with the wavelength-specific attenuation underwater, light becomes a complex, multidimensional and highly variable resource. Light fluctuations trigger functional responses in individual organisms and numerical responses in populations and communities, which propagate through the planktonic food web via the link between functional diversity and productivity. This dataset explored phytoplankton absorption properties and applied wavelet analysis on a timeseries of underwater irradiance measurements to explore dominant rhythmic, deterministic fluctuations in underwater light and the temporal scales at which they predominate.
evidence_items.title: Multiple dimensions of light shape phytoplankton trait diversity

evidence_items.summary: Objective of the study : to evaluate the clinical, anamnestic, reproductive, and hormonal characteristics of infertile patients with ovarian endometriomas depending on prior surgical treatment in assisted reproductive technology. Materials and methods . A retrospective cohort study was conducted involving 67 infertile patients who underwent evaluation and treatment using assisted reproductive technology programs between 2024 and 2026. Group 1 included 24 patients with ovarian endometriomas following surgical treatment; Group 2 included 23 patients with untreated ovarian endometriomas; and Group 3, the control group, included 20 patients with male-factor and/or absolute tubal infertility without endometriosis. Results . No statistically significant differences in age were found between the groups. At the same time, the groups differed in body mass index, age at menarche, and duration of infertility. Primary infertility was more common in patients with ovarian endometriomas, whereas secondary infertility predominated in the control group. Patients with endometriomas typically presented with dysmenorrhea and pre- and postmenstrual bleeding. The highest incidence of dysmenorrhea was observed in the group with untreated endometriomas. Regarding hormonal profile indicators, statistically significant differences were found in the levels of anti-Müllerian hormone and estradiol. The lowest anti-Müllerian hormone level was found in patients with endometriomas (0.61 ± 0.07 ng/mL), whereas in patients who had undergone surgical treatment it was 1.67 ± 0.28 ng/mL, and in the control group – 1.38 ± 0.14 ng/mL. Estradiol levels were highest in Group 2 – 143.5 ± 40.1 pg/mL. Conclusions . Infertile patients with ovarian endometriomas exhibit characteristic clinical and anamnestic features, including a higher prevalence of primary infertility, dysmenorrhea, and menstrual cycle disorders.
evidence_items.title: Clinical and anamnestic characteristics of infertile patients with ovarian endometriomas in assisted reproductive technology programs

evidence_items.summary: Objective of the study : to systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of adjunctive distrept-enzymes H46A streptokinase-streptodornase therapy in women with gynecological disorders and to interpret the available clinical evidence within the context of current concepts of inflammation, fibrinolysis, extracellular DNA, immunothrombosis, and adhesion biology. Materials and methods . PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, Europe PMC, ClinicalTrials.gov and additional sources were systematically searched from database inception through 2026 without language restrictions. The review followed PRISMA 2020 recommendations and was prospectively designed according to Cochrane methodology. Randomized controlled trials evaluating distrept-enzymes H46A streptokinase-streptodornase therapy in women with postoperative gynecological complications, pelvic inflammatory disorders, endometriosis-associated symptoms or related reproductive conditions were eligible. Primary outcomes included postoperative recovery, inflammatory resolution, pelvic pain, adhesion-related outcomes and reproductive preservation. Results . The review demonstrated consistent clinical improvements associated with adjunctive distrept-enzymes H46A streptokinase-streptodornase therapy across multiple gynecological settings. Compared with standard management alone, enzymatic therapy was associated with higher rates of complete hematoma resolution, greater reductions in C-reactive protein concentrations, faster functional recovery, improved quality of life, and clinically meaningful reductions in pelvic pain. Improvements in dyspareunia, dysuria and dyschezia were also observed among women with endometriosis-associated symptoms. No evidence suggested an increased frequency of serious adverse events, clinically significant bleeding or treatment discontinuation attributable to therapy.
evidence_items.title: Clinical efficacy and biological rationale of adjunctive distrept-enzymes H46A streptokinase-streptodornase therapy in gynecology: a systematic review with quantitative synthesis. Part I

evidence_items.summary: Preservation copy of an article published in International Journal of Current Trends in Research . Read the full article: https://ioro.org/ijctr/article/563942177632/563942177632 . Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming scientific research, environmental sustainability, healthcare, and intelligent infrastructure. However, conventional AI approaches often lack interpretability, cross-domain adaptability, and transparent decision-making. This study proposes an explainable multidisciplinary AI framework integrating predictive analytics, explainable AI (XAI), and multi-criteria decision analysis to support sustainable innovation across diverse research domains. The proposed framework combines Random Forest, XGBoost, and Explainable Boosting Machines with SHAP-based feature attribution and multi-criteria decision analysis. A comparative evaluation design considers environmental sustainability, healthcare, and intelligent infrastructure as representative application domains. Models are assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), explanation fidelity, computational latency, and decision consistency. Baseline comparisons include conventional machine learning without explanations, explainable models without decision optimization, and the integrated framework. Sustainability indicators, interpretability, computational efficiency, and decision robustness are incorporated into a unified evaluation protocol. Performance is compared using consistent data-splitting procedures, domain-specific metrics, and sensitivity analysis. The proposed framework establishes a measurable evaluation strategy for determining whether integrated explainability and decision optimization improve predictive reliability and practical decision support. Quantitative outcomes will include differences in predictive performance, explanation fidelity, latency, and decision consistency across models and domains.
evidence_items.title: Explainable Multidisciplinary Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Innovation and Intelligent Decision-Making Across Emerging Research Domains

evidence_items.summary: In the first quarter of the 21st century, the global trade system has entered a significant process of structural transformation as a result of intensifying geopolitical struggles, regional crises, logistic challenges emerging in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic, and supply chain disruptions caused by the Russia-Ukraine War. These developments have rendered international trade's dependence on certain critical transit points more visible, while increasing the need for the development of alternative transport corridors. This study aims to examine the potential impacts of the Development Road Project—which is planned to be implemented by Iraq, originating from the Grand Faw Port in Basra and reaching Europe via Turkey—on global trade networks, regional power relations, and Turkey's geoeconomic position within the framework of the neo-realist approach. Based on the qualitative research method, the study utilizes content analysis, comparative analysis, and geoeconomic evaluation techniques. The findings indicate that the Development Road Project has the capacity to strengthen Turkey's role as a transit country between Asia and Europe and elevate the country to the position of a major logistics hub. Nonetheless, the project faces various structural obstacles stemming from security-related risks, difficulties in securing financial resources, and the fragile political structure of the Middle East. Consequently, the study aims to contribute to the academic literature on the subject by evaluating the impact of logistics corridors on international relations from a neo-realist perspective.
evidence_items.title: The Impact of Iraq's Development Road Project on the Economies of the Region

evidence_items.summary: This record contains cleaned 10-minute SCADA data of 25 wind turbines at three wind farms, prepared for the article “Online state-space correction of transferred normal-behaviour models on new wind farms” (submitted to Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing). The turbines are 6 Senvion MM92 at Kelmarsh (UK, May–December 2016), 14 Senvion MM82 at Penmanshiel (UK, June–December 2016) and 5 turbines of EDP Wind Farm A (Portugal, about one year each), 557,562 rows in all. The data are derived from three public datasets: the Kelmarsh wind farm data (version 4, doi:10.5281/zenodo.16807551), the Penmanshiel wind farm data (version 0.0.2, doi:10.5281/zenodo.5946808), and Wind Farm A of the CARE to Compare dataset (doi:10.5281/zenodo.10958774; Gück et al., Data 9(12) 138, 2024). Each turbine is cleaned in five stages, in this order: removal of records missing a core signal and of out-of-range records; removal of logged stops and warnings (EDP: normal-operation records only); curtailment flags; a pitch-deviation filter; a power-outlier filter within wind-speed bins. Wind speed, power and rotor speed are given in original units and per unit of each farm’s rated values. Each record carries a gap-block identifier and an operating-regime label. Files: one compressed CSV per farm; the cross-validation splits used in the study; the per-unit reference values; make dataset.py , which rebuilds the data files from the raw releases row for row; a README that documents the sources, cleaning steps with row counts, columns, splits and known limitations. The EDP years are anonymised by the source. Licences: data CC BY-SA 4.0 (required by the EDP source data); code MIT. Please cite this record and the three source datasets.
evidence_items.title: Cleaned, per-unit 10-minute SCADA data from three wind farms (Kelmarsh, Penmanshiel, EDP Wind Farm A)

evidence_items.summary: Objective of the study : to evaluate the clinical effectiveness of complex non-pharmacological anti-stress therapy used as monotherapy and in combination with the herbal complex Tazalok in women with hypomenstrual syndrome, based on a comprehensive assessment of changes in menstrual function, ultrasonographic characteristics of the pelvic organs, quality-of-life indicators and laboratory evaluation of the hormonal profile over a six-month follow-up period. Materials and methods . The study included 100 women aged 18–40 years with hypomenstrual syndrome who were divided into two groups of 50 patients each. Women in Group I received non-pharmacological therapy for 6 months, including psychological support, lifestyle modification, nutritional correction, and optimization of physical activity. Patients in Group II additionally received Tazalok at a dose of 45 drops twice daily for 6 months. Clinical and ultrasound assessments were performed at baseline and after 1, 3, and 6 months of treatment. Serum levels of follicle-stimulating hormone, luteinizing hormone, estradiol, progesterone, prolactin, and cortisol were assessed, while quality of life was evaluated using the SF-36 questionnaire. Results . After 6 months of treatment, menstrual function was restored in 84% of patients in Group II compared with 70% in Group I. A regular menstrual cycle was observed in 78% and 52% of women, respectively (p < 0.05). According to ultrasound monitoring, ovulatory cycles after 6 months were detected in 60% of patients in Group II and 42% in Group I; however, the between-group difference did not reach statistical significance (p > 0.05). In contrast, laboratory-confirmed restoration of ovulation based on serum progesterone levels was observed in 68% of women in Group II versus 40% in Group I (p < 0.05).
evidence_items.title: Hypomenstrual disorders associated with chronic stress: non-hormonal treatment options

evidence_items.summary: Digital Twins of Qigong-Related Psychophysiological States at the Limit STARLI | White Rainbow Epoch Research Family | Flagship 20 This nonclinical research working monograph investigates what a defensible, transferable digital twin of qigong-related psychophysiological observations would have to predict, measure, and survive before it can claim incremental scientific value. The work couples Digital Twins, Qigong Physiology, and Transferable Models, with a central emphasis on day-ahead prediction and independent reconstruction. A qigong label here denotes a culturally situated breathing, attention, posture, or movement task; it does not establish an unrecognized form of physical energy. The scientific question is deliberately narrow: can a preregistered personalized model outperform a strong within-person historical baseline, on withheld future days and previously unseen breathing-by-movement conditions, for a traceable physiological endpoint such as ECG-derived NN-interval RMSE, while retaining reliable uncertainty calibration? A system that memorizes an individual's previous recordings, sees data from the future test day, relies on device or operator identity, or repeatedly recalibrates after the answer is revealed does not satisfy this claim. The work positions ECG R-peaks, normal-to-normal intervals, respiratory belts, inertial measurement units, peripheral electrodermal activity, temperature records, timing references, and instrument phantoms as candidate observations. These measurements are not interchangeable. A low prediction error on one sensor cannot license interpretation of a hidden mental or autonomic state that remains observationally indistinguishable from breathing rate, body movement, vigilance, posture, expectation, or shared sensor error. The book's measurement discipline begins with physical units and independent calibration.
evidence_items.title: Digital Twins of Qigong-Related Psychophysiological States at the Limit STARLI | White Rainbow Epoch Research Family | Flagship 20  This nonclinical research working monograph investigates what a defensible, transferable digital twin of qigong-related psychophysiological observations would have to predict, measure, and survive before it can claim incremental scientific value. The work couples Digital Twins, Qigong Physiology, and Transferable Models, with a central emphasis on day-ahead prediction and independent reconstruction. A qigong label here denotes a culturally situated breathing, attention, posture, or movement task; it does not establish an unrecognized form of physical energy.  The scientific question is deliberately narrow: can a preregistered personalized model outperform a strong within-person historical baseline, on withheld future days and previously unseen breathing-by-movement conditions, for a traceable physiological endpoint such as ECG-derived NN-interval RMSE, while retaining reliable uncertainty calibration? A system that memorizes an individual's previous recordings, sees data from the future test day, relies on device or operator identity, or repeatedly recalibrates after the answer is revealed does not satisfy this claim.  The work positions ECG R-peaks, normal-to-normal intervals, respiratory belts, inertial measurement units, peripheral electrodermal activity, temperature records, timing references, and instrument phantoms as candidate observations. These measurements are not interchangeable. A low prediction error on one sensor cannot license interpretation of a hidden mental or autonomic state that remains observationally indistinguishable from breathing rate, body movement, vigilance, posture, expectation, or shared sensor error.  The book's measurement discipline begins with physical units and independent calibration. An NN-interval RMSE is expressed in milliseconds under a fixed beat eligibility policy; respiration retains an appropriate physical or calibrated coordinate; skin conductance is recorded in microsiemens; movement amplitude and spectrum require an independently logged inertial unit; device timing and drift must be measured against a traceable reference. When observations share clocks, power supplies, contact artifacts, or environmental drivers, the cross-channel covariance must be retained rather than falsely decomposed into independent measurement errors.  The methodological proposal has five linked layers. Layer I is an operational contract that locks endpoints, sample units, eligibility, negative-control tasks, evaluation dates, and hard stops. Layer II is a measurement contract that documents raw signal provenance, physical units, sampling, calibration, cross-channel covariance, and uncertainty. Layer III is a hidden challenge program, including room changes, operator and device exchanges, sensor ablation, controlled respiratory pacing, and withheld breath-motion combinations. Layer IV requires a resource-matched comparison with the strongest conventional model available, including an autoregressive personal-history baseline and physiologically grounded respiratory predictors. Layer V calls for an independent laboratory to reconstruct the entire result and safety-abstention path from preserved raw traces and versioned analysis artifacts.

evidence_items.summary: Objective of the study : to evaluate the clinical utility of immunocytochemical assessment of MUM1 expression in liquid-based Pap tests for the diagnosis of chronic cervicitis. Materials and methods . Cytological specimens obtained from 50 women aged 23–60 years with inflammatory cervical lesions were examined. All patients underwent gynecological examination with cervical sample collection, conventional cytological evaluation by light microscopy, immunocytochemical staining using a monoclonal antibody against MUM1 followed by light microscopic assessment, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing for human papillomavirus (HPV), and microbiological testing for sexually transmitted pathogens. Colposcopy with cervical biopsy and subsequent histopathological examination were performed when clinically indicated. All patients received etiological treatment. Three months after the initiation of therapy, follow-up gynecological examination and repeat cytological assessment were performed. Results . According to the 2014 Bethesda System, all 50 patients were diagnosed with atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US). PCR testing confirmed HPV infection in only 8 (16.0%) women, whereas 42 (84.0%) patients were HPV-negative, indicating that the observed cytological abnormalities represented reactive changes associated with chronic inflammation rather than HPV-related epithelial lesions. Following etiological anti-inflammatory therapy and restoration of the normal vaginal microbiota, all HPV-negative patients were reclassified as negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM), confirming the inflammatory rather than HPV-associated origin of the cytological abnormalities. Immunocytochemical analysis demonstrated positive nuclear MUM1 expression in plasma cells in cases of true chronic cervicitis, with a mean of 1.14 MUM1-positive cells per 10 high-power fields, whereas no MUM1 expression was detected in patients with HPV infection.
evidence_items.title: The feasibility of immunocytochemical assessment of MUM1 marker expression in liquid-based Рap tests for the diagnosis of chronic cervicitis

evidence_items.summary: Objective of the study : To evaluate the effectiveness of combined therapy for cyclic mastalgia using a standardized extract of Vitex agnus castus BNO 1095 compared with magnesium therapy, alongside lifestyle modification and psychological support. Materials and methods . A total of 162 women of reproductive age with cyclic mastalgia were examined and divided into two groups. Group I (n = 79) received a standardized extract of Vitex agnus castus BNO 1095, presented as Agnus castus at a dose of 162 mg in combination with the phytocomponents Саulорhуllum thalictroides D4, Суclamen europaeum D4, Strychnos ignatia D6, Іrіs versicolor D2, Lilium tigrinum D3 as part of the complex herbal medicinal product Mastodinon® (Bionorica, Germany). Group II (n = 83) received magnesium citrate combined with vitamin B6. All participants underwent psychological counseling and lifestyle modification recommendations. The treatment duration was 6 months. Outcomes included pain intensity (NRS), sleep quality (PSQI), anxiety (GAD-7), depressive symptoms (PHQ-9), quality of life (SF-12), hormonal profile (prolactin, progesterone), and breast ultrasound characteristics. Results . In Group I, a statistically significant reduction in mastalgia intensity was observed (NRS: 7.24 ± 3.03 to 1.55 ± 1.47; p < 0.05), whereas Group II showed a less pronounced change (6.67 ± 4.33 to 4.87 ± 2.92). Anxiety levels (GAD-7) decreased significantly in Group I (7.88 ± 0.56 to 4.13 ± 0.61; p < 0.05), while no significant changes were observed in Group II. Sleep quality improved in both groups, but normalization of PSQI was more frequent in Group I. In the Vitex agnus castus group, a reduction in prolactin levels (33.55 ± 5.13 to 15.5 ± 3.12 ng/mL; p < 0.05) and an increase in progesterone levels (6.04 ± 4.01 to 16.56 ± 3.29 nmol/L; p < 0.05) were observed.
evidence_items.title: Optimization of treatment of cyclic mastalgia in women against psycho-emotional stress

evidence_items.summary: Diabetes mellitus remains a major global health challenge, necessitating the development of new therapeutic agents targeting key enzymes involved in carbohydrate metabolism. In this study, ten novel imidazo-thiazole-thiazolidinone hybrids were designed, synthesized and their structural integrity was confirmed through 1H NMR and 13C NMR along with mass determination by HREI-MS. After characterization, each derivative was subjected to in-vitro evaluation using acarbose (reference) to assess their anti-diabetic potential through the inhibition of key enzymes. Compound 3 and 6 with IC50 values 3.20 ± 0.20 μM, 2.10 ± 0.30 μM for α-amylase and 3.70 ± 0.30 μM, 2.60 ± 0.20 μM for α-glucosidase acted as the excellent inhibitors, markedly affecting rate of enzymatic reactions, with kinetic studies revealing their mode of inhibition. The SAR analysis revealed key substituents enhanced ligand-enzyme affinity, supported by molecular docking showing their specific binding. Furthermore, in-vivo cytotoxic assessment in rat models was performed to examine toxicological aspects and biocompatibility of synthesized compounds. Pharmacophore modeling, DFT calculations and MD simulations were also conducted to provide mechanistic insights. Comprehensive ADMET analysis including bioavailability, toxicity prediction, oral suitability and drug-likeness together with in-vivo safety evaluation complemented the in-vitro and computational findings, demonstrating these imidazo-thiazole based thiazolidinone derivatives hold promise as effective therapeutics against diabetes mellitus.
evidence_items.title: Interrogating imidazo[2,1-b]thiazole-4-thiazolidinone hybrids as antidiabetic leads: molecular cartography, pharmacokinetic profiling and rodent therapeutic response.

evidence_items.summary: During natural gas hydrate production in the Shenhu area of the South China Sea, water released from hydrate dissociation coupled with formation water, may induce water-locking, which blocks gas flow pathways and restricts productivity. To elucidate the mechanisms and potential remediation strategies, this study employed low-field NMR to systematically investigate the spatiotemporal evolution of water-locking in argillaceous silt hydrate reservoirs at initial water saturations of 50%, 70%, 90%, and 100%, and evaluated three antiwaterblocking agents (fluorocarbon types I and II, and nonionic surfactant III). Results show that water-locking predominantly occurs in micropores (T2 < 10 ms, pore size < 1 μm), with intensity increasing exponentially with saturation through four stages (end-face, mid-end combined, wide-area, and full-domain water-locking) identifying 70% saturation as the critical range for the tested material. Agents I and II perform effectively at low to moderate saturations, but their efficacy is severely limited at saturations ≥90% and under fully saturated conditions. Displacement pressure synergistically enhances agent performance, yet pressure alone is insufficient. This study clarifies the evolution mechanisms and application boundaries of chemical remediation, offering theoretical guidance for water-locking prevention and efficient hydrate development in the South China Sea.
